tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.title: List every AI model currently available
tools.description: List every AI model currently running on the Livepeer network — image, video, audio, 3D, voice/TTS, and finishing tools (cropping, stitching, watermarking). Use early in a session to see what's available before picking one. The list is live, so models the network adds or removes show up here first. Free.

kind.description: Filter to one capability kind (ai / tool / mcp).

limit.description: Max capabilities in structuredContent. Omit to return all; pass e.g. 50 on a large registry to stay well under token limits.

offset.description: Skip this many capabilities (with limit) for paging.

annotations.title: List every AI model currently available

tools.name: describe_capability
tools.title: Describe one capability (how to use it)
tools.description: Return the detail card for ONE capability — identity (kind/modality/family/aliases), metering unit + USD price, latency SLA, fallback chain, live availability, and a ready-to-run invocation example for the verb THIS surface registers. Use after list_capabilities to see exactly how to invoke a specific model before calling it. Free.

annotations.title: Describe one capability (how to use it)

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.title: Show what each model costs (USD rate card)
tools.description:
Show the USD price for every model on the network — images priced per megapixel, video per second, voice/TTS per 1,000 characters, finishing tools per call. Filter by model name or kind to narrow. The price shown is what the user actually pays; upstream provider cost + margin are disclosed where available. This is the rate card (pre-flight), not retrospective spend. Free to call.

USE WHEN: pre-flight cost question — 'how much will this cost', 'which model is cheapest for video', comparing premium vs budget options. These are rates, not spend. For 'what did I spend today / on flux-dev / this session', use get_cost_report instead.

kind.description: Filter by capability kind. Default 'all' returns every cap.

name.description: Optional capability name (e.g. 'flux-dev'). Returns just that row when set.

bypass_cache.description: Skip the 60s pricing cache and force a fresh fetch from the SDK service. Use when verifying a just-published price change or debugging stale-rate suspicions. Default false (use the cache).

annotations.title: Show what each model costs (USD rate card)

tools.name: list_checkpoints
tools.title: List Pending Checkpoints
tools.description: List checkpoint pauses for the bearer's recent jobs. Each entry is a (parent_id, checkpoint_id, completed/total, next_step_summary) tuple. Filter by project_id / parent_id / status / since. Use when an async tool returned `should_resubscribe: true` AND `pending_checkpoint_id` is set on the parent job (or simply poll periodically when you submitted with `checkpoint_every_n`).

project_id.description: Optional project filter — only return checkpoints whose parent job produced this project_id.

parent_id.description: Optional parent-job filter — only return checkpoints for this specific cjob/moodboard/place_subject id.

status.description: Optional status filter. 'pending_review' is the actionable subset — these are the checkpoints awaiting a resume decision.

since.description: Optional epoch-ms cutoff — only return checkpoints created at or after this timestamp.

tools.name: review_checkpoint
tools.title: Read Full Checkpoint State
tools.description: Read the full pause state for a checkpoint: completed slot URLs (partial_state) + pending-but-not-started scene prompts (pending_state) + the human review_prompt + allowed decision options. Use to render an inline review card or terminal prompt before deciding continue / edit / reshoot / abort.

checkpoint_id.description: Checkpoint id from list_checkpoints. Returns the full pause state (partial_state with completed slot URLs + pending_state with not-yet-started scene prompts + the human review prompt and allowed decision options).

tools.name: resume_from_checkpoint
tools.title: Resume a Paused Job from Checkpoint
tools.description: Apply a decision to a checkpoint and re-spawn the worker. Decisions: 'continue' (pending scenes as-is), 'edit' (rewrite pending scene prompts via the modification text), 'reshoot' (move a partial-state slot back to pending), 'abort' (mark parent failed; no further inference). Idempotent — second call with the same decision returns the cached child_parent_id. Pass `resume_token` from review_checkpoint to protect against double-resume from two browser tabs.

decision.description: What to do at this checkpoint. 'continue' resumes with the same pending scenes verbatim. 'edit' rewrites the pending scene prompts via the modification text (e.g. 'make the grandfather younger ~60s'). 'reshoot' takes a slot id in modification ('slot-3') and moves that slot from partial_state back to pending_state. 'abort' marks the parent job failed; no further inference.

modification.description: Decision-specific modifier. For 'edit': a free-form direction applied to all pending scenes. For 'reshoot': the slot ref ('slot-3'). For 'continue' / 'abort': ignored.

resume_token.description: Optional anti-replay nonce echo'd from the previous resume. Protects against double-resume from two browser tabs. When omitted, the first resume wins; locked_decision is captured for idempotent replay.

annotations.title: Resume a paused job from checkpoint

tools.name: subscribe_progress
tools.title: Stream Progress on an Async Job (notifications/progress)
tools.description:
Hold a tool call open for up to 25s, polling the target job every 2s, emitting MCP notifications/progress on each meaningful status change. Returns on terminal status or budget expiry. Supports mjob_* / cjob_* / ltj_* job ids (media / creative / lora-train). Non-terminal responses include `should_resubscribe: true` so the agent re-calls to continue streaming.

USE WHEN: a previous async submit returned a job_id and the agent wants to STREAM progress instead of polling get_create_media / get_creative_job / get_lora_train every 8-15s. The notifications/progress channel renders inline in Claude Cowork / Cursor / Claude Desktop UIs. Skip this for media jobs that finished synchronously (most image gen) — there's nothing to stream.

job_id.description: ID of a previously-submitted async job. Accepts: mjob_* (create_media async), cjob_* (submit_creative_job), ltj_* (submit_lora_train), atask_* (submit_agent_task), mood_* (moodboard_spread async). Re-subscribing after a 25s budget elapses is supported — the new call picks up where the old one left off.

budget_seconds.description: How long to hold this call open before returning (5-25s, default 25). Lower values reduce wall-clock latency between subscriptions but raise re-subscribe overhead. The tool ALWAYS returns by the budget; agents should re-call when status is still non-terminal.

annotations.title: Stream progress on an async job

tools.name: critique_shot
tools.title: Critique a Shot Against a Reference (Vision-LLM Drift Gate)
tools.description:
Grade how well a generated scene matches a reference (character anchor, brand kit reference, or earlier-scene canonical) using Gemini Vision. Returns 4 sub-scores (face / marks / wardrobe / palette) plus a weighted total + pass/fail vs the threshold (default 0.7).

USE WHEN: after a multi-scene render, verify a specific shot hasn't drifted from the anchor before shipping. Pair with the entity registry seeded by `generate_project` — pass `reference_url: <entity canonical_url>` and `generated_url: <new scene>`. The grader is PERMISSIVE on transient failures (no GEMINI_API_KEY, fetch error) — it returns `total: 1` so the gate never blocks shipping when the grader itself is broken. The agent should NOT treat permissive scores as endorsement; they mean 'couldn't grade, decide on other signals'.

generated_url.description: Public https:// URL of the scene to grade. Typically a result from create_media / generate_project. Must be reachable from the Livepeer Agent MCP server (generated-media URLs and Livepeer Agent storage are first-class).

reference_url.description: Public https:// URL of the canonical reference (character anchor sheet, first-scene snapshot, brand kit reference). The grader compares the generated scene against this image and scores face / marks / wardrobe / palette fidelity.

entity_name.description: Optional entity label (e.g. 'Grandpa Tom', 'Pure North bottle'). When set, surfaces in the response as `entity_name` for downstream logging / display. Doesn't change the grading — the vision LLM grades visual similarity, not name semantics.

threshold.description: Optional pass threshold for the weighted total. Default 0.7 (matches generate_project's internal retry threshold). The response always includes `pass: total >= threshold` so the agent can branch without re-applying the threshold themselves.

annotations.title: Critique a shot against a reference

tools.name: analyze_video_tracks
tools.title: Analyze Video — Track, Blur, Zone, Annotate, Heatmap (Supervision)
tools.description:
Run a Roboflow Supervision pipeline over a video. Returns an annotated MP4 (or overlay PNG for heatmap) PLUS a structured sidecar (tracks JSON / zone counts / dwell-time CSV) and a summary.

USE WHEN: you need TEMPORAL tracking (stable tracker IDs across frames), zone entry/exit counts, deterministic face/plate blur for compliance, or a movement heatmap. Distinct from `marlin-video` (semantic scene captioning, no IDs) and from `yolo-detect` (per-frame boxes only, no tracker continuity). Pick mode='track' as the default ByteTrack pipeline; 'blur' for pre-publish anonymization; 'zone'/'heatmap' for analytics.

DETECTOR DEPENDENCY: the default container ships detector-less (MIT license preservation). Modes 'track' / 'blur' / 'annotate' REQUIRE a `detections_url` (sidecar from a prior yolo-detect / yolo-segment call). 'zone' and 'heatmap' work off geometric primitives + tracker IDs and don't need detections.

PERSISTENCE: pass `project_id` + `scene_index` to write `{annotated_url, sidecar_url, summary}` onto that scene's blob so the viewer + downstream tools can surface the analysis without re-running.

video_url.description: Public https:// URL of the source video. Must be reachable from the Livepeer Agent MCP server; generated-media URLs and Livepeer Agent storage are first-class. 500 MB / 5 min hard caps enforced container-side.

mode.description: Which supervision-* capability to invoke. 'track' (default) runs ByteTrack across frames; 'blur' auto-blurs target classes (compliance gate); 'zone' counts entries/exits across polygon or line zones; 'annotate' applies named annotators using supplied detections; 'heatmap' accumulates an overlay PNG + per-zone dwell CSV.

detections_url.description: Optional per-frame detections JSON URL (sidecar from a prior yolo-detect / yolo-segment / roboflow-inference call). REQUIRED today for mode='track' / 'blur' / 'annotate' on the default detector-less container build. Not used by mode='zone' or 'heatmap' which work off geometric primitives.

classes.description: Optional whitelist of class names (e.g. ['person', 'car']). Detections outside this list are dropped before tracking. Class names must match what the upstream detector emitted; pass nothing to keep everything.

min_confidence.description: Minimum detection confidence (0-1). Detections below this score are filtered out before tracking / annotation. Default 0.35 — Supervision's documented sweet spot for ByteTrack stability.

annotators.description: Named annotators to overlay on the output video. Default ['box', 'label', 'trace'] for mode='track'. 'blur' / 'pixelate' force-anonymize; 'mask' / 'halo' need segmentation detections.

zones.description: Required for mode='zone' / 'heatmap'. List of polygon (≥3 points) or line (2 points) zones in pixel coordinates. Each zone gets entry/exit/dwell counted. Optional 'label' surfaces in the response summary.

smoothing_window.description: Optional DetectionsSmoother window in frames. 0 disables smoothing (default); 3-5 reduces jitter for shaky video at the cost of latency in tracker updates.

project_id.description: Optional project to persist the result onto. When supplied with `scene_index`, the annotated_url + sidecar_url + summary land on `scenes[scene_index].analysis` so the viewer and downstream tools can surface the analysis without re-running.

scene_index.description: Optional zero-based scene index within `project_id`. Ignored when project_id is absent. Required when project_id is set.

annotations.title: Analyze video — track, blur, zone, annotate

tools.name: submit_plan
tools.title: Propose or Execute a Multi-Step Plan (Plan→Act)
tools.description:
Bundle multiple tool calls into one approval gate. Propose mode (pass `steps`): server validates each step, estimates total cost, persists with status="proposed", returns a plan_id + per-step cost breakdown. NOTHING runs. Execute mode (pass `plan_id` + `confirm:true`): server marks the plan running and fires sequential execution in the background; poll get_plan for state.

USE WHEN: a workflow needs more than one tool (e.g. generate_project → create_media(action='publish') → ...) and the user / agent benefits from a single approval card showing total cost before any inference fires. Single-tool calls don't need this — just call the tool directly. Step types today: create_media (any action) and generate_project. Step outputs flow via the existing @last_image / @last_video / @last_audio symbols when downstream steps reference them.

PATTERN: 1) call submit_plan({steps:[...], goal:'...', budget_usd:...}) → get plan_id + cost. 2) surface to user / approve. 3) call submit_plan({plan_id, confirm:true}) → background execution starts. 4) poll get_plan({plan_id}) until status=done/partial/failed. The hard cap is 8 steps per plan; sequential execution (not parallel) so a step N output reliably reaches step N+1.

steps.description: Ordered list of tool calls (1-8). Required for the propose mode. Omit when executing a previously-proposed plan via plan_id+confirm.

tool.description: Which MCP tool this step invokes. Closed set today; create_media covers all single-asset actions (generate, animate, music, tts, mux_audio, lipsync, subtitle, upscale, publish, comfy_workflow); generate_project covers multi-scene narratives. To chain step outputs, use the @last_image / @last_video / @last_audio symbols in downstream steps' args — the resolver is shared with create_media.

args.description: Args forwarded verbatim to the tool. The shape matches the tool's own input schema (e.g. create_media expects {action, prompt, ...}). Validated server-side at propose time so the caller sees errors before approval.

label.description: Optional short label for this step. Appears in the approval card and get_plan responses (e.g. 'Generate 4 Ghibli scenes', 'Concat to MP4'). Pure cosmetics — has no effect on execution.

goal.description: Optional human-readable goal. Shows up in the approval card / status responses so reviewers can see what the plan is for at a glance.

budget_usd.description: Optional total budget cap. When set and the summed step costs exceed it, the plan is rejected at propose time with both numbers surfaced — the caller can trim steps or override by raising the cap.

quality_threshold.description: Forwarded onto every create_media step that doesn't supply its own quality_threshold. Default 0.7. Lets a plan-level approval set the bar once instead of per-step.

plan_id.description: When set, switches to execute mode. Must come from a previous propose call's response, and must be paired with confirm:true. The server marks the plan 'running' and fires sequential execution in the background.

confirm.description: Must be true to execute a proposed plan (paired with plan_id). Acts as the explicit approval gate — there is no other way to commit a plan to execution. Ignored in propose mode.

annotations.title: Propose or execute a multi-step plan

tools.name: get_plan
tools.title: Poll a Plan→Act Plan
tools.description:
Read the full state of a plan submitted via submit_plan: status, per-step status + URLs + quality scores + errors, total estimated and actual cost. Scoped to your bearer — other users' plan ids return not_found.

USE WHEN: after submit_plan({plan_id, confirm:true}), poll every ~8-15s until status transitions to done / partial / failed / cancelled. Also valid before approval to re-read the proposed plan (status=proposed).

plan_id.description: Plan id returned by submit_plan. Plans are scoped to your bearer — other users' plans return not_found even if you guess a valid id.

tools.name: critique_batch
tools.title: Critic Agent — Cross-Asset Review
tools.description:
Evaluate a batch of generated assets as a GROUP using a 'critic' persona (Gemini Vision multi-image). Returns verdict (ship/iterate/indeterminate), per-asset notes, cross-asset issues + missing pieces + strengths, plus concrete next_actions the agent can fire to fix what's wrong.

USE WHEN: after a multi-step generate_project or submit_plan landed N assets and you want a second-pair-of-eyes review before declaring done. Distinct from critique_shot (single image vs anchor) — this is the cross-asset / cross-narrative critic. Pass `urls` directly, OR `plan_id` to pull urls from a previously-executed plan's outputs. Permissive on grader failure (verdict=indeterminate, never blocks). Cost ~$0.01 per batch.

urls.description: 2-12 public asset URLs to review as a group. Either pass urls directly, or pass plan_id to pull the urls from a previously-executed plan.

plan_id.description: Plan id from submit_plan. The critic reads every step's output_url + output_urls[] from the plan and reviews them as a batch. Mutually exclusive with `urls`.

goal.description: Optional brief / goal the assets were generated to satisfy. Gives the critic a target to grade against — without this it can only assess consistency, not faithfulness.

brand_palette.description: Optional hex/named palette the assets should honour. When set, the critic adds a palette-fidelity dimension to its scoring.

focus.description: Where to spend grader attention. 'consistency' = character / wardrobe / palette across shots. 'completeness' = missing deliverables (audio, captions, final cut). 'fidelity' = each shot matches its share of the goal. 'all' (default) = balanced.

tools.name: replan
tools.title: Author a Recovery Plan from a Failed Plan
tools.description:
Given a plan that ended status='partial' or 'failed', build a NEW proposed plan that recovers from the failure. Three strategies: 'resume' (skip past the failed step), 'retry_with_delta' (replay with a refined prompt then continue), 'auto' (default — classifies the failure and picks for you). Output is always a fresh plan_id with status='proposed' so the existing approval gate fires before any recovery work runs.

USE WHEN: get_plan returned status='partial' or 'failed' and you want to recover automatically rather than authoring a new plan by hand. The classification surfaces in the response (transient / moderation / prompt / config) so the agent / human can decide whether to approve or rewrite. Config-class failures don't auto-replan — they need a human edit.

plan_id.description: The plan to recover from. Must be in status='partial' or 'failed' (replan on a 'done' or 'running' plan returns an error).

strategy.description: How to recover. 'resume' = skip past the failed step. 'retry_with_delta' = replay the failed step with a refined prompt, then continue. 'auto' (default) = pick based on the failure classification.

delta_prompt.description: Optional extra emphasis prepended to the retried step's prompt (only used when strategy ends up calling retry_with_delta). Lets the agent inject context the original prompt lacked — e.g. 'avoid named brands' for a moderation rejection.

annotations.title: Author a recovery plan from a failed plan

tools.name: get_scorecard
tools.title: End-of-Project Scorecard
tools.description: One-page aggregate report for a creative job (cjob_…) or a Plan→Act plan (plan_…). Aggregates: scene/step counts + success rate, quality scores from the inline gate (mean / pass-rate / retries used), critique verdict + issues from the auto-fired cross-asset critic, total estimated and actual cost, total wall time, and the viewer URL. Read-only — no new data collection, just a deterministic projection over existing storage. Use after a multi-scene render or a plan execution to render the report card for the user.

project_id.description: Creative-job id (cjob_…) or project id (proj_…) from generate_project / submit_creative_job. Mutually exclusive with plan_id.

plan_id.description: Plan id (plan_…) from submit_plan. Aggregates over plan steps instead of project scenes.

tools.name: get_cost_report
tools.title: Show what the marketer has spent recently
tools.description:
Show what the marketer has spent on Livepeer Agent over the last hour / day / 7 days, with an optional breakdown by model or status. Cost is the estimated USD captured at submission time from live pricing metadata. Free to call.

SCOPE: omit `scope` (or pass 'mine') and you get THIS key's spend — the answer to 'what did I spend'. Pass `scope: "session"` + the `session_id` you stamped on billed calls for one run's receipt. `scope: "all"` is the fleet total on a shared demo key; that scope is admin-gated and a normal key is denied.

USE WHEN: retrospective spend question — 'how much did I spend today', 'breakdown by model', 'what did this session cost'. This is spend, not rates. For pre-flight rate comparisons before generating, use get_pricing instead.

since.description: Time window, filtered by job creation time. 'all' returns every job on record — media jobs are NOT aged out, so this really does mean since-you-started, not a rolling window. Default 24h.

group_by.description: How to aggregate. 'capability' = per-cap totals; 'kind' = ai/tool/mcp totals (requires the job to carry that field); 'status' = done/failed totals; 'none' = single grand total only. Default 'capability'.

scope.description: Attribution scope. 'mine' (default) = only jobs submitted under YOUR bearer — the answer to 'what did I spend'. 'session' = only the spend tagged with the given `session_id` — the per-run receipt. 'all' = fleet total on a shared demo key; that scope is admin-gated and a normal key is denied. Pass session_id with scope='session'. Only calls made AFTER session tagging shipped match a scoped query.

session_id.description: Required when scope='session'. The same opaque tag you passed to create_media({ session_id }) for this run. Returns only that run's jobs.

limit.description: Max jobs to scan (default 200). Larger windows take longer to aggregate; cap protects MCP-client timeout.

annotations.title: Show what you have spent recently

total_cost_usd.description: LEDGER-NET spend in the window: reservations minus the corrections that released them. This is the number the 24h cap enforces against. Falls back to job-gross when the ledger is unreadable — cost_basis says which.

jobs_total_usd.description: JOB-GROSS: the sum of every job record's estimate, failures and cancellations included, before any release. Not comparable with total_cost_usd — use jobs_net_total_usd for that.

jobs_net_total_usd.description: LEDGER-NET: jobs_total_usd minus the releases on the ledger. The job-side figure that IS comparable with total_cost_usd.

released_usd.description: LEDGER-NET: how much reserved money came back in the window, as a positive number. A fact about your cap, not about the provider — a dispatched attempt is not refunded to us.

failed_cost_usd.description: JOB-GROSS: what the window's FAILED jobs were quoted at — the 'produced nothing' figure. Not netted by the release on purpose: the release is about your cap, the waste is about the work.

cancelled_cost_usd.description: JOB-GROSS: what the window's CANCELLED jobs were quoted at. Reserved and then released before delivery.

cost_basis.description: Which basis each money field above is on — ledger_net (reservations minus releases) or job_gross (estimates before any release). Computed, because total_cost_usd degrades to job_gross when the ledger is unreadable.

quality_credits_usd.description: LEDGER-NET: how much was credited back in the window for DELIVERED output that missed the quality bar after its retries. Distinct from released_usd, which is money for work never delivered at all. Absent when nothing was credited.

ledger_total_usd.description: LEDGER-NET: the raw ledger total this window, before the Math.max floor against jobs_net_total_usd.

job_records_total_usd.description: Alias for jobs_net_total_usd, paired by name with ledger_total_usd for the reconciliation.

unmetered_dispatch_usd.description: max(0, job_records_total_usd - ledger_total_usd): job records claiming spend the ledger has no matching entry for — i.e. an unmetered dispatch site. Decays to ~0 once every dispatch path reserves/settles against the ledger.

tools.name: create_media
tools.title: Make one image, video, or audio clip
tools.description:
Generate one image, video, or audio clip on the Livepeer network. Images come back in 3–30 seconds and the URL is returned right away. Video, audio, and 3D take 1–3 minutes — those return a job_id immediately and the agent polls get_create_media until done. Costs depend on the model: images ~$0.03–$0.10, video ~$0.05–$0.30, audio/TTS ~$0.01–$0.05.

USE WHEN: the marketer wants a single asset — one image, one short video, a voiceover clip — OR a discrete follow-up edit (restyle, animate, upscale, lipsync) on an existing asset. For 2+ scenes from one brief use generate_project. For a brand-exploration board (palette-driven, no narrative ordering) use moodboard_spread. For 'put this product in N different scenes' use place_subject. For 'show me 4 variations' use create_variations.

action.description: What to do. 'generate' = text-to-X (default routes to image; override with model_override for video/3D). 'animate' = image-to-video (needs source_url). 'music' = generate background music (needs prompt + duration). 'tts' = text-to-speech (prompt is the text). 'mux_audio' = lay ONE audio track onto a video, returns video (needs source_url + audio_url). 'mix_tracks' = mix N audio tracks (voice + music + sfx) into ONE audio file, returns audio (needs tracks; does NOT take a video — use mux_audio to put the result onto a clip). 'lipsync' = make an image / video lipsync to text or audio (needs source_url + (audio_url OR prompt)). 'subtitle' = burn captions onto a video (needs source_url; ASR coming, for now pass `text`). 'upscale' = 4× upscale an image (needs source_url). 'publish' = re-host source_url on Livepeer Agent storage and return a permanent public URL; needs source_url. 'comfy_workflow' = execute a Comfy API-format workflow JSON via Comfy Cloud (or future self-hosted Comfy); needs workflow_json.

prompt.description: Description / text. For generate: the visual brief. For music: 'cinematic premium reveal music'. For tts: the speech text. For lipsync: the speech text (TTS'd to a voice). For subtitle: the caption text (passed verbatim). For animate / mux_audio / upscale / publish / comfy_workflow: not used (default '.').

region_hint.description: Optional region preference for action='publish' or 'comfy_workflow' — e.g. 'us-east', 'eu-west', 'global'. Picks the cheapest tier-matching capability whose `regions` array includes the hint; falls back to global-tagged caps. Ignored for other actions.

workflow_json.description: Required for action='comfy_workflow'. The Comfy API-format workflow JSON exported from ComfyUI (Save → API Format). Forwarded verbatim to the upstream Comfy provider. See docs/design/comfyui-generalization.md.

workflow_inputs.description: Optional input override map for action='comfy_workflow'. The provider substitutes these into the workflow's input nodes before execution (e.g. {prompt: 'a cat', seed: 42}).

source_url.description: Required for animate / mux_audio / lipsync / subtitle / upscale. Accepts an explicit https:// URL, a recent-asset symbol ('@last', '@last_image', '@last_video', '@last_audio', '@last_3d'), a `gs://bucket/object` URI, OR an inline `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` attachment (auto-hosted to a public URL before dispatch; inline base64 is capped at ~3 MB — for larger/video files use upload / create_upload_url first). The server resolves symbols to the most-recent matching asset on your bearer. Use `get_recent_assets` to see what's available.

audio_url.description: Required for mux_audio (the audio to overlay) and optionally for lipsync (the speech audio to lip-sync to; otherwise the prompt is TTS'd). Accepts a URL or '@last_audio' / '@last' (recent-asset symbol).

end_image_url.description: Optional second keyframe for 'animate'. When the resolved model is ltx-i2v, veo-transition, or pixverse-transition, the model interpolates from source_url to end_image_url. Accepts a URL or '@last_image' / '@last' (recent-asset symbol).

voice.description: Optional voice id for tts / lipsync. Defaults vary by cap (chatterbox-tts has a friendly default voice). Pass to override.

tracks.description: Required for action='mix_tracks'. 1-8 audio tracks to mix into a single audio file. Each entry is either a bare URL string, or {url, volume?, delay_ms?} — volume defaults to 1.0, delay_ms to 0. Typical VO-over-bed: [{url: voice}, {url: music, volume: 0.35}]. Output is AUDIO (mp3); to lay the mix onto a video, feed the result to action='mux_audio'.

audio_fill.description: For mux_audio (ffmpeg-mux): fit the audio to the video length. 'loop' repeats a music bed so it covers the full video (use for a reel score so the audio doesn't stop before the video ends — the silent-tail fix); 'pad' extends with silence so the video is never truncated; omit / 'none' = leave lengths as-is.

text.description: Subtitle text for action='subtitle'. When omitted, ASR (auto-transcription) is used — currently not implemented; pass text explicitly until Wave 2 lands the ASR cap.

model_override.description: Force a specific capability (e.g. 'flux-dev', 'seedance-i2v', 'ltx-i2v', 'gemini-image'). Call list_capabilities to see options. Omit to let Livepeer Agent pick.

duration.description: Video duration in seconds (3-15). Used by i2v models. Per-model constraints (Livepeer Agent snaps automatically when possible): seedance-i2v / seedance-i2v-fast accept 4-15; ltx-i2v accepts only {6, 8, 10}; veo / kling / pixverse vary. Pass any value in 3-15 — the server snaps to the model's nearest valid bucket so calls don't fail on validation.

aspect_ratio.description: Optional target aspect ratio for image / video generation. Mapped per-capability: flux-dev / flux-schnell / recraft-v4 / gpt-image / gpt-image-edit → fal's `image_size` enum (square_hd, landscape_16_9, portrait_16_9, etc. — gpt-image-2 ignores the old gpt-image-1 `size` param); nano-banana → `aspect_ratio` direct passthrough (its fal API accepts the same string format). Video caps (ltx, ltx-q, kling-t2v) → `aspect_ratio` direct passthrough. Pixverse (default animate) and kling-i2v ignore the param — crop after with ffmpeg-export. Caps not in this list silently ignore the param today. Default 1:1 / square.

seed.description: Random seed for reproducibility — the determinism lever: same model + same prompt + same seed re-renders the same take, so you can change ONE thing per iteration and know what moved. Omit for a fresh random take (the response always echoes the seed that was used, so any result can be pinned after the fact). Passed through to the provider; a capability that does not accept seeds rejects it loudly rather than silently ignoring it.

lyrics_prompt.description: action='music' ONLY: the actual sung words, with [Verse]/[Chorus]/[Bridge]/[Outro] markup. Use `prompt` for STYLE (genre/bpm/mood), this for WORDS. For an instrumental bed, omit this (and `instrumental`) — music defaults to instrumental — or pass `[Instrumental]`.

instrumental.description: action='music' ONLY: force an instrumental (no-vocals) track. Defaults to true when neither `lyrics_prompt` nor `instrumental` is given — so a bare music call (style prompt only) returns an instrumental bed instead of erroring.

html.description: model_override='hyperframes-render' ONLY: the overlay HTML/CSS to composite over the AI background video (pixel-perfect text / UI / charts — fixes generative 'mushy text'). Position with absolute CSS; CSS animations work. Pair with background_video_url (or source_url) for the AI canvas + aspect_ratio for the dimensions.

html_url.description: model_override='hyperframes-render' ONLY, and PREFERRED over `html`: a handle to the overlay document, fetched server-side before dispatch. `logo_composite` returns one — pass it straight through. Use this rather than `html` whenever the overlay embeds an asset as base64: relaying that document through your own context corrupts it past roughly 26 KB, silently, from the bottom of the image up. Public https only, 200 KB cap. Ignored when `html` is also given.

background_video_url.description: model_override='hyperframes-render' ONLY: the AI-generated VIDEO used as the fullscreen background canvas behind the HTML overlay (its audio is muxed in). Must be a real video file — it is mounted in a <video> element, so a still image renders as a black frame; animate the still first. Defaults to source_url if omitted.

lora.description: Apply a trained LoRA to image generation. Get weights_url + trigger from list_loras. Only takes effect with action='generate' on flux-dev / flux-schnell (flux and flux-portrait LoRAs) or krea-2-lora (Krea 2 Open-Source LoRAs); ignored otherwise. The trigger is auto-prepended to the prompt; scale defaults to 0.7.

context_kit_id.description: Optional ContextKit / brand kit to lock onto. When set, the server prepends the kit's palette + prompt_keywords to the prompt automatically and (if the kit has lora_refs) attaches the kit's LoRA — so every asset for the same campaign carries the same brand signature. Get a kit_id from `brand_kit_create` / `context_kit_list`. The lock is per-call (no session sticky yet — Wave 2 will add `set_active_brand_kit`).

use_style_profile.description: Opt in to the saved style profile (`get_style_profile` / `rate_result`). Default FALSE: stored preferences are NEVER prepended to a prompt unless asked for. Preferences are stored per API KEY, and a key is a credential — on a shared or re-issued key the saved 'usual look' may belong to a different project or person, so applying it by default leaked one project's creative direction into another. Pass true when this really is the same person's ongoing work.

project_id.description: Optional project to attach this generation to. When set, the server consults the project's entity registry (characters / props / settings first registered by `generate_project`); if the prompt mentions a registered entity AND the project has consistency_priority enabled, the call auto-routes through kontext-edit with the entity's canonical reference URL as image_url. The resulting URL is then registered as a new sighting of any unregistered entities mentioned, so subsequent shots in the same project stay visually anchored. Has no effect when no entities match. When you also want the result written back onto a project SCENE (so director_export stitches it), target the scene with `scene_index` — or, for `animate`, pass the scene's current keyframe as `source_url` and the server matches it automatically.

cast.description: One way to keep a character consistent, and to have it VERIFIED. Pass { reference_url, name?, lock? }. On create_media it attaches the reference the way the browser's face lock does: image actions route through kontext-edit with the reference as the edit source; 'animate' starts the clip on the reference frame. On submit_creative_job / generate_project it feeds the graded character-anchor pipeline (every scene is scored against the reference and drifted scenes are re-rendered). An explicit model_override, source_url, or character_anchor always wins over cast, and the response says so.

name.description: Optional label for this character/subject — e.g. 'Mara'. Recorded for readability in disclosures and scorecards; it does NOT affect routing (routing is driven by reference_url + lock).

reference_url.description: Absolute https:// URL of the canonical reference image for this character / product / subject. SSRF-checked with the same guard character_anchor uses (https only, no IP literals, no local or metadata hosts).

lock.description: What the reference locks. 'face' (default) and 'full' both route image generation through kontext-edit with the reference attached, and i2v from the reference as first frame. 'style' does the same for image generation but does NOT become an i2v first frame — a style plate is not a keyframe.

scene_index.description: Optional zero-based scene position to write this result back onto (requires project_id). When set, the produced url + capability replace that scene's asset so `director_export` stitches the new asset (e.g. the animated clip) instead of the old keyframe. If omitted for an `animate` call, the server falls back to matching the scene whose current url equals `source_url` (the keyframe you animated). Out-of-range indices are ignored (the generation still succeeds and returns its url).

async.description: If true, return a job_id immediately and run the inference server-side. Poll get_create_media(job_id) for the URL. Auto-enabled for action='animate' and any video / 3D / audio model — those run 60–180s on fal and exceed most MCP clients' tool-call timeout. Set to false explicitly only on fast image models.

on_i2v_timeout.description: What to do when a video / animate job fails or times out on the GPU provider. 'fallback' (default for async/unattended runs) = automatically fetch a real stock b-roll clip matching the prompt so the reel never stalls; the result is tagged fallback_fired:{from,to,reason,reversible:true} and the caller should tell the user it's a stock substitute and offer 'redo with AI'. 'wait' = do not auto-substitute; surface the failure so an interactive agent can ask the user how to proceed (this is the right setting for interactive chat — the agent asks, then either retries AI or calls stock-footage-fetch itself). 'ask' is treated like 'wait' server-side (the asking is the agent's job).

max_cost_usd.description: Optional pre-flight budget cap in USD. If set, the server estimates cost from live pricing (display_price_usd × estimated units) and rejects the call before submission when the estimate exceeds this cap. Useful for batch agents that must stay under a per-task budget. The actual cost is persisted on the job and visible via get_cost_report.

prefer_fast.description: When true and no `model_override` is set, route to a faster sibling model: 'generate' → flux-schnell (~2s vs flux-dev's ~30s p75 under load), 'animate' → pixverse-i2v (warm, ~48s, ~100% success). The fast siblings carry lower fidelity — use when wall-clock matters more than stylization (chat preview, real-time iteration, draft moodboards). Set to false (or omit) for premium-quality default routing. (Note: fast animate was TEMPORARILY re-routed off seedance-i2v-fast on 2026-07-20 — it had no warm capacity and only ~33% success at the 180s ceiling; still reachable via model_override.)

respect_limits.description: When true, pause before inference if the ask hits a known model/tool limit (exact logos in pixels, publish-to-Slack/Drive, >15s continuous video, exact face across many shots without a reference). Default omit/false = soft-warn: still render, but structuredContent.feasibility explains the limit + workarounds. Opt in for honest pause-before-spend.

quality.description: Latency/quality tier for the render (video actions). 'fast' ≈ ≤90s (animate → pixverse-i2v); 'balanced' ≈ ~2min (animate → kling-v3-turbo-i2v); 'hq' = best-effort premium, may take 3–6min (animate → kling-o3-i2v). When omitted, animate defaults to pixverse-i2v (the fast tier) — the fastest i2v cap; other actions default to their balanced cap. Maps to a capability BEFORE model resolution; `model_override` still wins. Response carries eta_seconds/eta_p95_seconds/quality_tier so you can show the user an ETA and offer a re-render in a higher tier.

idempotency_key.description: Optional idempotency key. When set, a second call with the same key within 24h returns the cached result (with `idempotency_replay: true` in structuredContent) instead of re-running inference. Use for retry-safe flows: network-flaky tool boundaries, agents on at-least-once delivery, batch resumption. Scope: per-bearer. Format: 1–128 chars, A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - only. Generate one per logical action (e.g. crypto.randomUUID()).

quality_gate.description: Auto-evaluate the output against the prompt with a Gemini Vision grade. DEFAULT OFF (opt-in): omit for the fast interactive path — the grade adds several seconds of latency, so it no longer runs unless you ask for it. Set true to grade. With max_quality_retries>0 (default 1) the grade runs SYNCHRONOUSLY and regenerates on a low score (blocks until done). With max_quality_retries:0 (evaluate-only) the grade runs ASYNCHRONOUSLY — the image is returned immediately and the verdict is logged as a follow-up (quality.deferred:true in the response). Always auto-skipped on video/audio/3D/finishing kinds. Passing quality_anchor_url implies a grade.

quality_threshold.description: Pass threshold for the quality gate, 0..1. Default 0.7 (matches generate_project's existing drift gate for character_anchor scenes). Below this triggers a retry (up to max_quality_retries). Higher = stricter (more retries fire); lower = lighter touch.

max_quality_retries.description: Number of automatic retries when quality_gate flags a low score, 0..2. Default 1 (so total attempts = 2: original + one retry). Pass 0 to disable retry while still surfacing the quality score (evaluate-only mode). Hard-capped at 2 so a stuck prompt can't multiply cost beyond 3× the base inference.

quality_anchor_url.description: Optional reference image URL. When set, the quality gate switches to anchor-comparison mode (face/marks/wardrobe/palette sub-scores via the same Gemini Vision grader generate_project uses for character_anchor scenes) instead of generic prompt-match. Use when you have a canonical character or brand reference and want cross-shot consistency.

session_id.description: Optional per-run/session tag for cost attribution. Stamped onto the persisted job so `get_cost_report({ scope: 'session', session_id })` returns ONLY this run's jobs and its total reconciles with what you created — legible even on a shared demo key where every caller's bearer collapses to the same hash. Reuse one id for all calls in a logical run (e.g. crypto.randomUUID()). Format: 1–128 chars, A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - only.

persist.description: Re-host the final asset to durable storage and return a permanent URL instead of one that inherits the provider's lifetime. Adds a small storage cost and one copy step (the asset is downloaded server-side and re-uploaded, ≤ 50 MB), so it is off by default. On success the response's `url` is the durable copy, `persisted` is true, and `source_upstream_url` carries the original. If the copy fails the render still succeeds — you get the normal URL plus a `persist_failed` warning.

annotations.title: Make one image, video, or audio clip

cost_paid_usd.description: What the render actually cost, when the provider reported its metered units: billable_units × our published per-unit rate for the capability that ran. ABSENT/null means not known (pre-deploy adapter, or an unpriced capability) — never free.

billable_units.description: The provider's own billed quantity, kept raw beside cost_paid_usd so the multiply can be re-derived rather than trusted. Present only when the provider reported it.

served_model_id.description: The provider model id that actually served this render. Present even when it matches what we dispatched — that match IS the evidence the named-model guarantee held.

upstream_substitution.description: Present ONLY when served_model_id differs from the model we dispatched to. Should never appear: fal's silent fallback is disabled on our adapter. If you see it, the output came from a model you did not choose — report it.

budget_headroom_usd.description: USD left under your 24h spend cap. On create_media / run_capability: after this call's reservation. On submit_creative_job: before the job starts spending (it reserves per scene as it renders). ABSENT means unknown (unpriced capability, or the ledger could not be read) — never unlimited.

tools.name: get_create_media
tools.title: Check on a video or audio clip that's still rendering
tools.description: Check on a video or audio clip that's still rendering. Returns the current status (queued / running / done / failed), the final URL once it lands, or the error message if it failed. Sub-second per call, so polling at 5–10s intervals is safe. Free.

job_id.description: Job ID returned by create_media when running on the async path. Format: mjob_<12 hex chars>.

annotations.title: Check on a clip that's still rendering

error_code.description: Typed failure kind for a `failed` job — the same code the synchronous path returns inline. Null means NOT RECORDED, which is unknown, never 'not billed'.

error_retryable.description: Whether re-issuing this call could plausibly succeed. Surface-specific by design: on a create_media job a retry re-enters the fallback chain and may reach a sibling; on a run_capability job it re-issues the identical model.

error_billing_note.description: Whether the PROVIDER was billed for the failed attempt: not_billed_pre_dispatch | not_billed_upstream_5xx | likely_billed_upstream. Says nothing about your daily cap — cost_disposition answers that.

cost_disposition.description: What cost_usd_estimated currently IS: spent (delivered) | reserved (still in flight) | released (proven back on the ledger) | not_reserved (unpriced capability, nothing held) | demo_reconciled (credited back on the demo ledger) | release_failed (a release was attempted and did NOT land — you may still be holding it) | release_pending (no release recorded on this job).

spend_release.description: The recorded evidence behind cost_disposition: { attempted, reconciled?, delta_usd?, reason?, at }. Null when the terminal path recorded none.

cost_paid_usd.description: What the render actually cost, when the provider reported its metered units: billable_units × our published per-unit rate for the capability that ran. ABSENT/null means not known (pre-deploy adapter, or an unpriced capability) — never free.

billable_units.description: The provider's own billed quantity, kept raw beside cost_paid_usd so the multiply can be re-derived rather than trusted. Present only when the provider reported it.

served_model_id.description: The provider model id that actually served this render. Present even when it matches what we dispatched — that match IS the evidence the named-model guarantee held.

upstream_substitution.description: Present ONLY when served_model_id differs from the model we dispatched to. Should never appear: fal's silent fallback is disabled on our adapter. If you see it, the output came from a model you did not choose — report it.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.title: Cancel a job
tools.description: Stop an async job you no longer want. Takes the job_id from create_media / run_capability (mjob_*) or submit_creative_job / generate_project (cjob_*). The job's record goes terminal (status 'cancelled'), no worker will pick it up again, and the budget reservation it was holding is released so it stops counting against your 24h cap. Cancelling an already-cancelled job is a safe no-op. HONEST LIMIT: this does not yet reach the provider — a render already executing upstream may still finish, and we absorb that cost, not you. Free.

job_id.description: The job to cancel: an `mjob_*` id (from create_media or run_capability running async) or a `cjob_*` id (from submit_creative_job / generate_project). The id you were handed by the submit call.

tools.name: get_recent_assets
tools.title: Show the marketer's last 50 generated assets
tools.description: Show the last 50 images, videos, and audio clips the marketer has generated on this account, newest first. Use at the start of a follow-up turn — 'animate the last image', 'put the bike from earlier in a new scene' — instead of asking them to repaste URLs. Each entry has a short id (e.g. asset_a1b2c3d4) plus symbolic shortcuts (@last, @last_image, @last_video, @last_audio) you can reference directly. Cap of 50 entries; older items roll off as new ones land. Use forget_assets to clear early. Free.

limit.description: How many entries to return (most-recent first). Default 20, max 50.

kind.description: Filter to one media kind. 'image' covers t2i + edit + bg-removed; 'video' covers i2v + t2v + lipsync + talking-head; 'audio' covers music + sfx + tts. Omit for all kinds.

since_minutes.description: Only return assets generated within the last N minutes. Useful for follow-up turns scoped to the current session.

tools.name: forget_assets
tools.title: Clear the recent-assets memory (privacy)
tools.description: Clear the recent-assets memory so the marketer's history isn't visible to future chats. Default is a dry-run that previews 'would forget N assets' — pass confirm=true to actually wipe. Safety rule: confirm=true requires a bound via since_minutes and/or keep_urls (unbounded wipes are refused). Optionally scope to recent entries only (last 60 minutes, last 24 hours, etc.), and/or specify exact URLs to keep. Use when the marketer asks 'clear my history', 'forget what we just made', or wants privacy before sharing a session. Note: this only clears the index — image URLs themselves stay live until they age out at the upstream host.

since_minutes.description: Forget assets newer than this many minutes ago. Use 60 for 'forget the last hour', 1440 for 'last 24h'. REQUIRED for confirm=true — keep_urls alone does not satisfy it (see keep_urls below).

keep_urls.description: Exact media URLs that must be kept (never forgotten) within the since_minutes window. Exact-string match after alias-resolution (an aliased public URL and its raw upstream form both match). NOT a bound on its own — confirm=true still requires since_minutes; keep_urls only refines within it.

confirm.description: Safety latch — must be explicitly `true` to perform the wipe. Default `false` returns a dry-run preview of what would be removed. Requires since_minutes to be set (D-5: keep_urls is a keep-list, not a scope, and cannot substitute for a time bound).

tools.name: search_assets
tools.title: Search the marketer's recent assets
tools.description:
Find earlier images, videos, or clips by searching the prompt text, the asset type (image / video / audio), or a time window like '60 minutes ago' / '24 hours ago' / '7 days ago'. Returns each match with its short id, URL, original prompt, and creation time. Searches the marketer's last 50 assets. Free.

Use when the marketer says 'pull up the warm-amber moodboard from last Tuesday' or 'find the bike video I made earlier'.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring match against the asset's recorded prompt. Omit to list all recent assets (use kind + since to narrow instead).

since.description: Time window. Either a relative string ("60m", "24h", "7d") or an absolute epoch-ms number as a string. Omit for no time filter (the full 50-entry cap is your bound).

source_tool.description: Filter by which MCP tool produced the asset. Useful for 'show me everything I uploaded' vs 'everything the agent generated'.

limit.description: Max results (default 20; the registry holds 50 max).

offset.description: Skip the first N hits for pagination. Default 0.

tools.name: generate_project
tools.title: Render a multi-scene story or storyboard (2–30 scenes)
tools.description:
Render 1–30 ordered scenes from a single brief into a shareable viewer URL — storyboards, illustrated decks, mini-films, multi-shot pitches. Scenes render in parallel. Recurring characters and props are detected automatically so they stay consistent across scenes (the agent uses an image-edit model for follow-up scenes to preserve identity). Each scene gets its own URL, and the whole project gets a public viewer link the marketer can share.

USE WHEN: one brief produces 2+ ordered scenes that share characters, settings, or a narrative arc (storyboards, illustrated decks, mini-films, multi-shot pitches). For a single image use create_media. For a brand-exploration board (palette-driven, no narrative ordering) use moodboard_spread. If any scene needs video, use submit_creative_job (async) so the call doesn't hold the chat open for minutes. Consistency here is ATTEMPTED, not verified — nothing grades the result. When it matters that it actually held, either pass `verify: "on"` or use submit_creative_job. After this returns, subsequent create_media calls with the same project_id auto-route recurring entities through the image-edit path to keep them consistent.

title.description: Short title for the project. Shown on the viewer page.

prompt.description: Visual description for this scene. ~30 words works best; hard limit 4000 characters. Note that image models stop reading at roughly 2000 characters, so prose beyond that is accepted but unlikely to affect the render.

source.description: Where this scene's footage comes from. 'ai' (default) = generate via the model. 'stock' = fetch a real pre-shot clip from the stock library (Pexels/Pixabay) using `prompt` as keywords — instant, zero GPU, never times out. Use 'stock' for generic b-roll / cutaways; 'ai' for hero/character/product shots. A hybrid reel mixes both. Equivalent to model_override='stock-footage-fetch' but reads as intent.

scenes.description: Array of scenes (1-30). The agent should plan these from the user's brief — title + visual prompt per scene.

style.description: Optional global style suffix appended to every scene's prompt (e.g. 'cinematic, warm lighting'). Hard limit 600 characters.

global_model_override.description: Default capability for every scene (overridden per-scene if scene has model_override).

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio for EVERY scene (e.g. '9:16' for vertical TikTok/Reels/Shorts, '16:9' cinema, '1:1' square). Threaded to each scene's create_media. IMPORTANT: for a vertical short-form reel you MUST set this — without it scenes render at the model's default (square/landscape) and the whole reel ends up the wrong shape. Mapped per-capability the same way create_media maps it (flux/recraft/gpt-image → image_size enum, video caps → passthrough).

brief.description: Original user brief — stored alongside the project for context.

delivery_promise.description: What this project is committing to deliver. Omit to auto-classify from `brief`/`style` (default 'hybrid' if nothing matches). 'motion_led' = quality depends on real motion — the finished project is checked for a real-motion majority, and the response flags it if it isn't. 'source_led' = real/stock footage is the primary medium — scenes without an explicit model_override or source default to 'stock' (the free, zero-GPU stock-footage-fetch path) instead of AI generation. 'data_explainer' = visualization-first, stills are fine. 'hybrid' = no strong commitment (legacy behavior). The response always includes `delivery_check` showing the actual motion ratio against the promise.

context_kit_id.description: Optional ContextKit / brand kit to lock onto. When set (or when an active brand kit is pinned via set_active_brand_kit), the kit's palette + prompt_keywords are prepended to EVERY scene's prompt so the whole project carries the same brand signature. Same shape as create_media's context_kit_id (D1/D2 in moodboard-cowork-ux plan).

async.description: Sync vs async behavior. 'auto' (default) returns a job_id for video models or >4 scenes; otherwise renders sync. 'always' forces async. 'never' forces sync (will time out on long jobs).

verify.description: Grade every rendered scene against the character anchor and re-render what drifted. 'on' always verifies; 'off' never does; 'auto' (the default) verifies only when an anchor exists AND there are 3+ scenes — the point at which drift starts to be both likely and expensive to spot by eye. Costs one vision call per scene (a few seconds, ~$0.002) and is bounded by a project-wide retry budget, so a bad batch cannot run away. Consistency is ATTEMPTED without this; it is VERIFIED with it.

character_anchor.description: Cross-shot character consistency control. Omit (undefined) for the recommended default: 'auto' kicks in when scenes.length >= 3 (multi-shot stories benefit from the anchor; 1-2 scene calls render independently for speed). 'off' forces independent renders even on long stories — distinguishing marks will drift across shots. 'auto' extracts characters from the brief, generates a character sheet via nano-banana, and uses it as a reference image for every scene — fine details (white paw, scarred ear, hair streaks) carry across shots. 'always' forces auto behavior even on 1-2 scene calls. Or pass an absolute https:// URL to use a pre-existing character sheet image (URL is SSRF-checked: must be https, no IP literals, no metadata/local hosts). Equivalent to `cast: { reference_url }` — this field takes precedence when both are set.

cast.description: One way to keep a character consistent, and to have it VERIFIED. Pass { reference_url, name?, lock? }. On create_media it attaches the reference the way the browser's face lock does: image actions route through kontext-edit with the reference as the edit source; 'animate' starts the clip on the reference frame. On submit_creative_job / generate_project it feeds the graded character-anchor pipeline (every scene is scored against the reference and drifted scenes are re-rendered). An explicit model_override, source_url, or character_anchor always wins over cast, and the response says so. Here it is exactly equivalent to `character_anchor: <reference_url>` and reaches the same graded pipeline (verified when `verify` is on/auto). An explicit `character_anchor` wins.

name.description: Optional label for this character/subject — e.g. 'Mara'. Recorded for readability in disclosures and scorecards; it does NOT affect routing (routing is driven by reference_url + lock).

reference_url.description: Absolute https:// URL of the canonical reference image for this character / product / subject. SSRF-checked with the same guard character_anchor uses (https only, no IP literals, no local or metadata hosts).

lock.description: What the reference locks. 'face' (default) and 'full' both route image generation through kontext-edit with the reference attached, and i2v from the reference as first frame. 'style' does the same for image generation but does NOT become an i2v first frame — a style plate is not a keyframe.

wait_minutes.description: Maximum time the user is willing to wait, in minutes (1-10, default 4). Drives the pre-flight budget router: when the agent picks a slow premium model (e.g. gpt-image) for a multi-scene project that wouldn't fit in this budget, the router auto-downgrades to a fast model (flux-dev) with a stylization-preserving suffix. Pass a higher value (and/or include 'high quality' in the brief) to keep gpt-image even on long projects.

confirm.description: Cost-preview safety latch (H1). Default `true` — runs the project. Set to `false` for a dry-run that returns the resolved capability per scene, total estimate, and budget-router decision without firing inference.

checkpoint.description: LEAP #2 — preview-first rendering. 'keyframes' renders a cheap still per scene FIRST (video models are swapped for a fast image cap during this phase; image models render normally), pauses the run with a Z6 checkpoint, and returns the keyframe URLs inline for review. Resume via resume_from_checkpoint: 'continue' animates each approved keyframe with the requested video model (or finalizes the project as-is for image models), 'edit' prepends a direction to every pending scene before the finish pass, 'abort' cancels with no further spend. The keyframe phase always renders synchronously (it IS the inline preview); the finish pass runs in background — poll get_creative_job for progress. Omit for the classic single-pass render.

mode.description: Director execution mode for the PRE-FINISH gate (after all scenes render, before delivery). 'autopilot' = never pause, ship in one call (user is certain). 'director' = always pause for human review before delivery. 'auto' = ship UNLESS the auto-critic is unsure (score < confidence_threshold, verdict 'iterate', or a flagged shot) — best-of-both default. OMIT for legacy straight-through behavior. NOTE: setting mode FORCES async execution (returns a job_id) — the gate lives in the async worker — overriding async:'never'. Threaded to submit_creative_job; resume via review_checkpoint + resume_from_checkpoint.

confidence_threshold.description: Only used when mode='auto'. Overall critique score at or above this ships; below it escalates to a human pre-finish gate. Default 0.8.

tools.name: merge_projects
tools.title: Combine 2–5 projects into one (optionally stitch the videos)
tools.description:
Combine the scenes from 2–5 existing projects into one new project with its own viewer URL. Scenes are re-numbered in order and every original prompt and URL is preserved. Optionally also stitch all the video scenes together into a single MP4 deliverable (poll the resulting job to get the final video). If there aren't enough videos to stitch, the call still succeeds — the stitch step is skipped with a friendly note. Free except for the optional stitch step.

Use when the marketer has built scenes across multiple sessions and now wants one combined deck or video.

project_ids.description: 2-5 project ids returned by generate_project / submit_creative_job. Scenes are concatenated in the order given and re-numbered 1..N.

title.description: Title for the merged project. Defaults to the first source project's title.

brief.description: Brief for the merged project. Defaults to the first source project's brief.

tools.name: submit_creative_job
tools.title: Render a multi-scene project that includes video (async)
tools.description:
Render a multi-scene project — returns a job_id immediately and renders server-side over a few minutes. Poll get_creative_job for per-scene progress and the final viewer URL.

USE WHEN: consistency has to be VERIFIED, not just attempted — a recurring character, product or world where it would be a real problem if it changed between shots. This is the only verb that renders a reference anchor, grades every frame against it (face, marks, wardrobe, palette) and re-renders what drifted, then pauses before delivering if the batch critic is unsure. ALSO required for video, 8+ scenes, or auto_plan.

PREFER generate_project when speed matters more than proof: it keeps recurring entities consistent through an image-edit path and holds the call open, but nothing checks whether that worked.

── SAY WHAT YOU WANT, OR IT CANNOT HONOUR IT ──
Four things are NOT inferred from a brief, because guessing them would change the cost of every job that didn't mean it. If the user implied any of them, pass it:
  • `target_duration_sec` — 'a minute long', 'about 30 seconds'. Divided across the scenes and clamped to 3-15s per shot, so ~60s over 6 scenes becomes 10s each. Rule of thumb: scenes ≈ seconds / 10. Without it you get whatever each capability's default clip length is, which is usually much shorter than the ask.
  • `deliver: "reel"` — the user wants A VIDEO, not a gallery. Default 'scenes' returns a viewer page with each shot as its own asset; 'reel' also stitches one file with a soundtrack and returns `reel_url`. If the request sounds like a finished piece ('a documentary', 'an ad', 'a trailer'), pass this.
  • `quality: "fast"|"balanced"|"hq"` — pass 'hq' for anything a client sees, 'fast' for a look still being decided. Omitted, the brief is read for a standard ('cinematic'/'4K'/'broadcast' → hq; 'draft'/'quick'/'rough' → fast). Note an explicit draft word BEATS a quality adjective, so 'quick cinematic sketch' resolves to fast — pass `quality` outright if the user meant otherwise.
  • `aspect_ratio` — '9:16' for vertical/TikTok/Reels, '16:9' for landscape.

── WHAT IT DECIDES FOR YOU ──
Do NOT hand-pick capabilities to get the right medium; the delivery promise does it. A brief reading like a documentary/cinematic piece auto-classifies `motion_led` and routes untagged scenes to a text-to-video model at the resolved quality tier; an infographic/explainer brief routes to the infographic model; 'real footage only' routes to stock. Pass `delivery_promise` explicitly only to override that reading. An explicit `global_model_override` or per-scene `model_override` always wins, and every substitution is reported in `warnings`.

── THE HIGHEST-VALUE MOVE ──
Pass your OWN `scenes` array rather than `auto_plan:true`. The planner writes prompts, not shots — it never picks capabilities, durations or a runtime. Supplying scenes keeps your writing AND still gets the anchor grading, the drift retries and the finishing. Name the cast explicitly in every scene prompt and restate wardrobe; the grader compares against a reference, so give it one worth comparing to. Use `auto_plan` only when the user has a brief but no shot list.

── QUALITY AND REVIEW GATES ──
  • `shot_strategy: "keyframe_then_animate"` — render a still per scene, then animate THAT still. A curated first frame constrains composition and palette for the motion that follows; a straight text-to-video pass re-invents them each shot. Costs one extra image render per scene. Reach for it when framing or cross-shot consistency matters more than speed.
  • `keyframe_review: true` (with the strategy above) — pause after the stills and BEFORE the video spend. Stills cost cents, motion costs dollars, so this is the cheapest possible place to catch a miss. The job writes a checkpoint and exits; call review_checkpoint to see the stills, then resume_from_checkpoint. Choosing 'edit' there re-renders that still to match the new prompt rather than animating the frame the user was trying to change.
  • `checkpoint_every_n` — pause every N finished scenes. Best on 8+ scene projects to gate late spending.

── THE APPROVAL CARD IS NOT NOISE ──
Most real jobs come back `status:"awaiting_confirmation"` with `cost_confirm`. Show the user its `line_items` (the capability and cost PER SCENE), the total, and `predicted_motion_ratio`, then approve with `submit_creative_job({job_id, confirm:true})`. Read it rather than approving blind: an unexpectedly CHEAP estimate on a video brief is the classic sign the plan is about to render stills. A job whose plan contradicts its promise is staged no matter how little it costs.

── READING THE RESULT ──
`status:"partial"` means a scene FAILED — it is not a quality note. Everything that rendered is safe in the project, so recover with director_re_render / director_insert on that project; re-submitting the brief pays for the finished scenes a second time. `delivery_check` says whether the finished mix matched what the brief promised, with the remedy if not. `warnings` lists every substitution, fallback and shortfall — relay it; if this verb chose something for the user, it is written there. `reel_url` is the single finished file when `deliver:"reel"` was set.

title.description: Short title for the project. Shown on the viewer page. Required when submitting a NEW job; omit it when approving a staged job with job_id+confirm (the staged job already stored its title).

scenes.description: Array of scenes (1-30). Either supply this directly, or set auto_plan:true with a brief.

prompt.description: Visual description for this scene. ~30 words works best; hard limit 4000 characters. Note that image models stop reading at roughly 2000 characters, so prose beyond that is accepted but unlikely to affect the render.

duration.description: Seconds for THIS shot. Video capabilities quantize to whole seconds and most cap near 15, so a long piece is made of more shots rather than longer ones. Omit to let the job's target_duration_sec divide evenly, or the capability's own default apply.

quality.description: Quality tier for THIS shot, overriding the job's. Same tiers as create_media.

auto_plan.description: If true, expand `brief` into scenes via Hermes before rendering. Ignored when `scenes` is provided.

generation_mode.description: Default 'auto': for a short (2-6 shot) single-style brief, routes to Kling 3.0's model-native multi-shot (ONE inference call, ≤15s total) instead of per-scene orchestration — better continuity, one render instead of N. Falls back to 'scenes' automatically on any native failure or when the brief doesn't qualify (8+ scenes, per-scene model overrides, stock-footage jobs, an explicit non-generic video model). Pass 'scenes' to force today's orchestrated fan-out; pass 'native' to force the native attempt (surfaces a failure instead of silently falling back).

scene_count.description: Target scene count when auto_plan is true (default 6).

style.description: Optional global style suffix appended to every scene's prompt (e.g. 'cinematic, warm lighting'). Hard limit 600 characters.

global_model_override.description: Default capability for every scene. For text-to-video use a TEXT-to-video cap ('ltx-t2v', 'veo-t2v', 'kling-v3-turbo-t2v', 'seedance-mini-t2v') — NOT an image-to-video cap like 'seedance-i2v' (those need a source frame). 'flux-dev' for image. (An i2v cap picked for a text scene is auto-swapped to its t2v sibling.)

brief.description: Original user brief — stored alongside the project. Required when auto_plan is true.

agent_id.description: Optional marketplace agent slug. When set, the worker loads the agent's manifest and uses its system_prompt + byoc_capability defaults; the resulting job is tagged with this agent_id for rating attribution.

character_anchor.description: Phase 1 of the consistency improvement plan: cross-shot character consistency control. 'off' (default for backward compatibility) renders each scene independently. 'auto' extracts characters from the brief, generates a character sheet via nano-banana, and uses it as a reference image for every scene. 'always' forces auto behavior even on short stories. Or pass an absolute https:// URL to use a pre-existing character sheet image (URL is SSRF-checked). Equivalent to `cast: { reference_url }` — this field takes precedence when both are set.

cast.description: One way to keep a character consistent, and to have it VERIFIED. Pass { reference_url, name?, lock? }. On create_media it attaches the reference the way the browser's face lock does: image actions route through kontext-edit with the reference as the edit source; 'animate' starts the clip on the reference frame. On submit_creative_job / generate_project it feeds the graded character-anchor pipeline (every scene is scored against the reference and drifted scenes are re-rendered). An explicit model_override, source_url, or character_anchor always wins over cast, and the response says so. Here it is exactly equivalent to `character_anchor: <reference_url>`: the anchor sheet, the per-scene drift grading and the re-render budget are the ones that already ship. An explicit `character_anchor` wins.

name.description: Optional label for this character/subject — e.g. 'Mara'. Recorded for readability in disclosures and scorecards; it does NOT affect routing (routing is driven by reference_url + lock).

reference_url.description: Absolute https:// URL of the canonical reference image for this character / product / subject. SSRF-checked with the same guard character_anchor uses (https only, no IP literals, no local or metadata hosts).

lock.description: What the reference locks. 'face' (default) and 'full' both route image generation through kontext-edit with the reference attached, and i2v from the reference as first frame. 'style' does the same for image generation but does NOT become an i2v first frame — a style plate is not a keyframe.

budget_router_log.description: Internal: pre-flight budget-router decision text from generate_project. Surfaced into the async worker's consistency_log so users can see the auto-downgrade trace.

checkpoint_every_n.description: Z6 — Pause for human review after every N completed scenes. The worker writes a StoredCheckpoint and exits; caller polls list_checkpoints + calls review_checkpoint + resume_from_checkpoint to continue. Omit (default) for legacy fire-and-poll behavior — no pauses, full project renders straight through. Best for 8+ scene projects where the user wants gates before late spending. Honored by submit_creative_job today; moodboard_spread / place_subject parity lands in Z6.1.

auto_critique.description: After all scenes complete with ≥2 successes, automatically run critique_batch with all successful scene URLs + the brief + brand palette and attach the verdict to the job. Default true. Set false to skip the post-fanout critic (saves one Gemini Vision call, ~$0.01). Skipped when only 1 scene succeeds or GEMINI_API_KEY is unset.

mode.description: Director execution mode for the PRE-FINISH gate (after all scenes render, before delivery). 'autopilot' = never pause, the critic auto-resolves — one call, finished artifact out (use when the user is certain). 'director' = always pause for human review before delivery (ignores the critique signal — every gate is a human gate). 'auto' = ship UNLESS the auto-critic is unsure: overall score < confidence_threshold, verdict 'iterate', or any flagged shot (per_asset.ok=false) — the best-of-both default; needs auto_critique on (the default) to have a signal, and with no signal it ships. OMIT for legacy behavior: no pre-finish gate, the job completes straight through. Independent of checkpoint_every_n (the mid-fanout count gate).

confidence_threshold.description: Only used when mode='auto'. Overall critique score at or above this ships; below it escalates to a human pre-finish gate. Default 0.8. Lower = ship more aggressively; higher = pause more often.

quality.description: Quality tier for every scene that doesn't set its own — the same tiers create_media takes. Omit and the tier is read from brief/style ('cinematic', '4K', 'broadcast' => hq; 'draft', 'quick', 'rough' => fast); a brief expressing no standard leaves each capability's default alone. A per-scene `quality` and an explicit `model_override` both win over this.

target_duration_sec.description: Total runtime you want, in seconds. Divided across the scenes and clamped to what capabilities accept (3-15s per shot), so ~60s over 6 scenes becomes 10s each. If the scene count can't reach it the response says so instead of quietly delivering a different length. A per-scene `duration` wins over this.

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio for every scene. Matches generate_project's field.

shot_strategy.description: How each video scene is rendered. 't2v' (default) = one text-to-video pass per scene. 'keyframe_then_animate' = render a still first, then animate THAT still — a curated first frame constrains composition, palette and framing for everything the video model does after it, where a bare t2v pass re-invents them per shot. It also lets you see cheap stills before the video spend. Costs one extra image render per scene, which is why it is opt-in. Ignored for image-only scenes.

keyframe_review.description: Pause after the keyframes and before the video spend, so you can look at the stills first. Requires shot_strategy:'keyframe_then_animate'. The job renders one still per scene, writes a checkpoint and exits; call review_checkpoint to see them, then resume_from_checkpoint to animate — 'edit' a prompt there and that scene's still is re-rendered to match rather than animating the frame you were changing. This is the cheap-artifact-first gate: stills cost cents, the motion costs dollars.

deliver.description: What to hand back. 'scenes' (default) = a viewer URL with each scene as its own asset, today's behavior. 'reel' = ALSO stitch the scenes into one file with a soundtrack and return its URL, so the job produces a deliverable rather than a gallery. Best-effort: a finishing failure still delivers the scenes and warns.

delivery_promise.description: What this project commits to deliver — see generate_project's `delivery_promise` for the full contract. Usually passed through automatically when generate_project delegates here for >4-scene / video-model jobs. Under 'source_led', scenes without an explicit model_override default to the free stock-footage-fetch path. Omit to auto-classify from brief/style.

budget_usd.description: Hard ceiling in USD for THIS job's estimated cost. Checked before anything is staged or dispatched: if the plan's estimate is over it, the call is REFUSED with code 'budget_exceeded' and returns the estimate, your budget, the largest scene_count that would fit, and the cheaper routes — the scenes are never silently trimmed to fit, because a 6-scene story cut to 3 is a different story. When the plan fits, the response echoes `budget_usd` and `budget_remaining_usd`. This is your plan's constraint; it is not the 24h wallet cap (see spend_cap) and not create_media's per-asset max_cost_usd. The figure it compares against is an ESTIMATE — 'auto_plan_heuristic' basis is coarser than 'explicit_scenes'.

job_id.description: When set, switches to execute mode: approves and starts a job that the cost-confirm gate previously staged as awaiting_confirmation. Must be paired with confirm:true. Ignore this field when submitting a NEW job.

confirm.description: false = quote-only on a NEW job (no persist, no dispatch). true + job_id starts a job the cost-confirm gate staged. Omit on a new job to submit (the gate still stages when the estimate is ≥ $0.50 or ≥ 8 scenes).

session_id.description: Optional per-run tag for cost attribution. Stamped onto every scene render so `get_cost_report({ scope: 'session', session_id })` returns this job's spend. Same format as create_media({ session_id }).

budget_headroom_usd.description: USD left under your 24h spend cap. On create_media / run_capability: after this call's reservation. On submit_creative_job: before the job starts spending (it reserves per scene as it renders). ABSENT means unknown (unpriced capability, or the ledger could not be read) — never unlimited.
