tools.name: apply_lora
tools.title: Apply a Trained LoRA
tools.description: Generate an image with a trained LoRA applied. Pass weights_url + trigger from list_loras (or copy from the Livepeer Agent UI's /lora list). The trigger token is auto-prepended to the prompt. Image only — video/edit base models reject LoRA weights.

prompt.description: Text prompt. The LoRA's trigger token is auto-prepended.

weights_url.description: URL of the LoRA weights file. Get this from list_loras or the training job result.

trigger.description: The trigger token the model expects. Auto-prepended to the prompt.

model.description: Inference cap. Defaults to flux-dev. Use krea-2-lora, flux-2-lora, qwen-2512-lora for matching train bases; wan-22-i2v-lora / wan-22-t2v-lora for video LoRAs (i2v vs t2v must match train base).

source_url.description: Required for wan-22-i2v-lora — hero keyframe image URL to animate with the video LoRA.

train_base.description: Optional guard: reject if model does not match the LoRA's train base (wan i2v/t2v mismatch).

tools.name: submit_lora_train
tools.title: Submit a LoRA Training Job (Async)
tools.description: Kick off LoRA fine-tuning on a ZIP of images. Returns a job_id immediately; the SDK runs server-side for 10–20 min. Poll with get_lora_train. On completion the trained LoRA is auto-mirrored — list_loras + apply_lora pick it up without any browser involvement.

zip_url.description: URL to a ZIP of training images. Must be on an approved host — call `upload` (or `create_upload_url` for large files) and pass the URL it returns.

trigger_word.description: Token that will activate the LoRA at inference time (e.g. 'MOCHI_DOG'). Auto-uppercased.

display_name.description: Friendly name for the resulting LoRA (defaults to trigger_word).

base_model.description: Base model to train against. Default flux-dev. Use 'krea-2' for aesthetic/style LoRAs (infer on krea-2-lora). Use 'flux-portrait' for face/likeness (infer on flux-dev). Use 'flux-2' for FLUX.2 realism + text (infer on flux-2-lora). Use 'qwen-2512' for product/packaging with strong text (infer on qwen-2512-lora). Use 'wan-22-i2v' for product-to-video i2v LoRA (infer on wan-22-i2v-lora + source keyframe). Use 'wan-22-t2v' for text-to-video scene LoRA (infer on wan-22-t2v-lora).

steps.description: Training steps. Default varies by base (400 for wan video, 1000 flux, 2500 portrait). Wan video allows 100–20000; flux-portrait up to 10000; others up to 4000.

learning_rate.description: Optional per-trainer learning rate (portrait, flux-2, qwen-2512, wan video).

auto_scale_input.description: Wan video trainers only (wan-22-i2v / wan-22-t2v). Scale clips to 81 frames @ 16fps. Default true.

tools.name: get_lora_train
tools.title: Get LoRA Training Status
tools.description: Read the status, progress, and (when complete) weights_url of a job submitted via submit_lora_train. Auto-resumes polling if the prior background worker hit its function-side deadline.

tools.name: attach_lora_to_project
tools.title: Attach a LoRA to a Project
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants the same trained character / style LoRA to apply to every generation in a project (e.g. 'use Mochi as the protagonist for all scenes'). Persists to a per-bearer attachment index. Accepts lora_id OR lora_name. Pass detach:true to undo. Response surfaces weights_url + trigger so the agent can pass them to create_media until auto-injection ships.

lora_id.description: LoRA id. Use this OR lora_name; lora_id wins if both given.

project_id.description: Project id to bind the LoRA to.

detach.description: If true, detach the LoRA from the project instead of attaching.

annotations.title: Attach a LoRA to a project

tools.name: list_lora_attachments
tools.title: List LoRA → project attachments
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user asks 'what LoRA is active for project X' or 'where am I using Mochi'. Returns the full lora_id → project_ids map, or filtered to one project_id.

project_id.description: Filter to LoRAs attached to this specific project. Omit for the full map.

tools.name: voice_create
tools.title: Create a Named Voice
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to keep a reusable named reference to a vocal sample (a host voice, a narrator, a brand voice, a personal voice memo). Stores `{name, source_audio_url}` in the per-user voice library so the agent can later look it up by name and pass `audio_url` explicitly on a `chatterbox-tts` call. SKIP for one-off TTS where the user passes audio_url directly. NOTE: this PR ships the library only — `chatterbox-tts` does NOT yet auto-receive audio_url from an attached voice. A follow-up wires the auto-injection; until then, the agent reads the voice via voice_list and passes audio_url explicitly. Confirmed 2026-05-28: upstream chatterbox accepts audio_url as the voice-clone reference.

name.description: Friendly name. Use kebab-case ('narrator-warm', 'host-energetic') so they're easy to reference by name.

source_audio_url.description: Public audio URL (mp3/wav/m4a). 5-30s is ideal — too short = drift, too long = the model only uses the first chunk anyway.

sample_text.description: Optional sample text the catalog can use to render a preview clip.

attach_project_id.description: Optional project to attach immediately. Equivalent to a follow-up voice_attach call.

tools.name: voice_list
tools.title: List Saved Voices
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user asks 'which voices do I have' or the agent needs to pick a voice by name before passing its audio_url to a chatterbox-tts call. Returns saved voices from the per-user library; pass `project_id` to filter to voices attached to a specific project. Per-user; only voices saved under your API key are visible.

project_id.description: If set, return only voices attached to this project. Otherwise return all voices for the user.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Pass the `next_cursor` from a previous response to fetch the next page.

tools.name: voice_attach
tools.title: Attach a Voice to a Project
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to remember which voice goes with which project, so later voice_list calls filtered by project_id return the right voice without re-attaching by name every time. Binds a saved voice ↔ project_id (many-to-many). Pass `detach: true` to undo. Accepts voice_id or voice_name (case-insensitive). NOTE: auto-injection into chatterbox-tts is a follow-up — for now this is bookkeeping; the agent still reads the attached voice via voice_list and passes audio_url explicitly.

voice_id.description: Voice id. Use this OR voice_name; voice_id wins if both given.

project_id.description: Project id to bind the voice to.

detach.description: If true, detach the voice from the project instead of attaching.

annotations.title: Attach a voice to a project

tools.name: get_style_profile
tools.title: Read the user's accumulated style preferences
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user asks 'what's my style', or BEFORE passing `use_style_profile: true` to create_media so you can show them what would be added to the prompt. Returns prefs from rate_result keeps/picks (and any browser mirror). Preferences are stored per API KEY and are NEVER applied to a prompt unless a render explicitly opts in — on a shared or re-issued key the saved look may belong to someone else. Pass `clear: true` to wipe after a brand pivot.

category.description: Filter to one preference category. Default 'all'. Use this when the agent only needs preferred-models for routing vs preferred-styles for prompt prefixes.

clear.description: If true, wipe the profile after reading — ONLY the scope you read. Scoped clears are why this is safe now: the old behaviour wiped the whole API key, which broke any other project still using that key.

project_id.description: Read (or clear) the preferences saved for ONE project. Preferences saved with `rate_result({ project_id })` live here, not on the key.

session_id.description: Read (or clear) the preferences saved for one run/session.

tools.name: rate_result
tools.title: Remember what the user liked or disliked
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user says 'I like this', 'keep #2', 'not that style', or picks a numbered next_actions option that implies taste. Records the preference; it is NOT applied to later prompts unless a render passes `use_style_profile: true`. Free — no inference. Keep the note to an aesthetic ('soft daylight', 'muted palette') — do NOT store subject matter (a character, a prop, a specific object), which would insert that thing into unrelated frames.

signal.description: keep = user liked this result; reject = disliked / regenerate; pick = chose this among options (e.g. menu #2).

note.description: Optional short taste note to remember — e.g. 'soft daylight', 'muted palette', 'editorial'. Stored as a style preference.

value.description: Explicit preference value when you already know it (overrides note). e.g. 'watercolor', 'cinematic teal'.

project_id.description: Save this preference to ONE project instead of to the API key. Strongly preferred: a key-scoped preference is visible to every holder of that key, and unlimited/demo keys get re-handed-out — that is how one project's creative direction leaked into another's renders.

session_id.description: Save this preference to one run/session instead of to the API key. Use when there is no project yet but the taste is specific to this piece of work.

annotations.title: Remember what the user liked or disliked

tools.name: list_templates
tools.title: Browse named creative recipes (with prices) and campaign starters
tools.description:
Browse the named creative recipes — camera moves (dolly-in, 360° orbit, crane reveal, FPV drone sweep…), delivery formats (vertical hook, product packshot loop, lower-third explainer) and looks (watercolour storybook, teal-and-orange, Kodak Vision3) — each with what it costs, priced live. Also lists the moodboard brief starters for campaign flows. Filter with kind ('recipes' / 'moodboard' / a domain) and category ('camera' / 'format' / 'look'). Free.

Use when the user asks for a named move or look ('give it a dolly-in', 'make it feel like film'), asks what presets exist, or asks 'where do I begin'. Then apply_recipe({ recipe_id, subject }) shows the exact call and the price before anything renders.

kind.description: Which catalog to list. 'all' (default) = priced creative recipes + moodboard brief starters. 'recipes' = only the named, priced camera / format / look presets. 'moodboard' = only the marketer brief starters. The four domain values (brand / community / game / personal) filter the MOODBOARD catalog by domain, as before.

category.description: Filter the RECIPE catalog: 'camera' = named camera moves (dolly-in, orbit, crane…), 'format' = delivery shapes (vertical hook, packshot loop), 'look' = grades and painting styles. Ignored for moodboard templates.

annotations.title: Browse named recipes and campaign starters

tools.name: export_recipe
tools.title: Export a Project as a Portable Recipe
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to share their project with a teammate, save a workflow for reuse, or fork their own work into a variant. Returns the project's title + brief + style + scenes (prompts only — fresh renders on import) as a JSON recipe. Source URLs and entity registry preserved on export; import drops the URLs so the recipient renders their own.

project_id.description: Project to export as a recipe. Project must exist under your bearer.

annotations.title: Export a project as a portable recipe

tools.name: apply_recipe
tools.title: Apply a Named Recipe — a Priced Preset, or a Shared Project
tools.description:
Two modes, one verb.

CATALOG PRESET — pass recipe_id + subject (from list_templates({kind:'recipes'})): expands the named camera move / format / look into the exact create_media call and tells you what it costs, WITHOUT rendering. The caller confirms via next_actions. USE WHEN the user names a move or look ('dolly-in on the espresso machine', 'watercolour storybook version').

PROJECT SNAPSHOT — pass recipe (a JSON from export_recipe or a teammate): creates a new project with empty scene URLs; pass the new project_id to generate_project to fan out renders. USE WHEN the user pastes a recipe JSON.

Not to be confused with apply_template, which applies a moodboard brief starter.

recipe.description: PROJECT-recipe mode. The recipe object returned from export_recipe. Creates a NEW project with fresh scenes; original output URLs are NOT preserved (the recipient renders their own). Mutually exclusive with recipe_id.

recipe_id.description: CATALOG-recipe mode. The id of a curated priced preset from `list_templates({ kind: 'recipes' })` — e.g. 'dolly-in-push', 'product-packshot-loop', 'watercolor-storybook'. Returns the expanded create_media call plus its live price for you to confirm; renders NOTHING on its own. Mutually exclusive with recipe.

subject.description: CATALOG-recipe mode only: what the preset is applied TO — the thing being filmed, photographed or painted (e.g. 'a matte-black espresso machine on a walnut counter'). Fills the recipe's {subject} slot; the rest of the prompt is the preset's fixed direction.

source_url.description: CATALOG-recipe mode only, and only for a camera / format preset (those animate an existing frame): the still to move the camera on. Accepts an https URL or a recent-asset symbol. Defaults to '@last_image' — your most recent image — so the returned call is runnable as-is.

title_override.description: Optional new title. Default reuses the recipe's title.

render.description: If true, fan out and render every scene immediately via generate_project. Default false — create the project metadata only, scenes stay empty until the agent invokes them.

annotations.title: Apply a named recipe — priced preset or shared project

tools.name: director_re_render
tools.title: Re-render One Scene of a Project
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user has a generated project (from generate_project / submit_creative_job) and wants ONE specific scene re-prompted while the rest stay locked — e.g. 'shot 3 should have the character running instead of walking'. Reuses the project's entity registry (character LoRA, brand kit) automatically. Use scene_index from the viewer (0-based). Omit prompt to regenerate with the same prompt (useful after a failed render).

use_style_profile.description: Opt in to the saved style profile for this render (see create_media's field of the same name). Default false — stored preferences are never prepended unless asked for, because they are keyed on the API key rather than the project.

project_id.description: Project id (from generate_project / submit_creative_job).

scene_index.description: Zero-based scene position in project.scenes. Get via the viewer or get_creative_job.

prompt.description: Optional new prompt. When omitted, the scene's stored prompt is re-used verbatim.

action.description: create_media action. When omitted: 'animate' if the stored scene is already video (capability/url), otherwise 'generate' (text-to-image). Pass explicitly to force either path. Use 'animate' with the current scene URL as source when re-animating a still.

model_override.description: Optional capability override (e.g. 'flux-dev', 'kontext-edit'). When omitted, the agent + entity registry pick.

prefer_fast.description: When true and no model_override, route to fast siblings (flux-schnell / pixverse-i2v). Default false. (Fast animate was TEMP re-routed off seedance-i2v-fast on 2026-07-20 — see create_media.prefer_fast.)

quality.description: Quality/latency tier passed straight through to create_media (fast=pixverse-i2v-class <90s, balanced=default, hq=kling-o3-i2v-class premium). model_override still wins. This is what the webapp Studio ⚡/💎 tier toggle threads in. Omit for the balanced default.

cast.description: One way to keep a character consistent, and to have it VERIFIED. Pass { reference_url, name?, lock? }. On create_media it attaches the reference the way the browser's face lock does: image actions route through kontext-edit with the reference as the edit source; 'animate' starts the clip on the reference frame. On submit_creative_job / generate_project it feeds the graded character-anchor pipeline (every scene is scored against the reference and drifted scenes are re-rendered). An explicit model_override, source_url, or character_anchor always wins over cast, and the response says so. Here it is passed straight through to create_media, so re-rendering one shot can hold the same character the rest of the project holds. The response's `cast` block says whether it applied.

name.description: Optional label for this character/subject — e.g. 'Mara'. Recorded for readability in disclosures and scorecards; it does NOT affect routing (routing is driven by reference_url + lock).

reference_url.description: Absolute https:// URL of the canonical reference image for this character / product / subject. SSRF-checked with the same guard character_anchor uses (https only, no IP literals, no local or metadata hosts).

lock.description: What the reference locks. 'face' (default) and 'full' both route image generation through kontext-edit with the reference attached, and i2v from the reference as first frame. 'style' does the same for image generation but does NOT become an i2v first frame — a style plate is not a keyframe.

annotations.title: Re-render one scene of a project

tools.name: director_insert
tools.title: Insert a New Scene Between Two Existing Ones
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants ONE NEW scene added between two existing project scenes — e.g. 'add a transition shot between 2 and 3, character walking through a doorway'. Pass between=[a, a+1] where a is the predecessor scene's zero-based index. Use [-1, 0] to prepend at the start, [N-1, N] (N = total scenes) to append at the end. The new scene inherits the project's character LoRA and brand kit automatically.

use_style_profile.description: Opt in to the saved style profile for this render (see create_media's field of the same name). Default false — stored preferences are never prepended unless asked for, because they are keyed on the API key rather than the project.

project_id.description: Project id (from generate_project / submit_creative_job).

between.description: Adjacent scene-index pair [a, b] where b === a + 1. New scene lands at b; every scene at index >= b shifts up. Use [-1, 0] to prepend, [N-1, N] to append (N = total scenes).

title.description: Optional human-friendly title for the inserted scene.

action.description: create_media action. Default 'generate' (text-to-image). animate only works when the new scene chains off the previous scene's URL via a follow-up call.

prefer_fast.description: When true and no model_override, route to fast siblings. Default false.

annotations.title: Insert a new scene between two others

tools.name: director_retime
tools.title: Trim or Extend a Scene's Duration
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to adjust a single video scene's length — head trim ('cut 0.4s off the start'), tail trim ('trim 0.4s off the end'), or absolute target ('make this exactly 4s', 'make this 8s — loop if needed'). Exactly one of head_offset / tail_offset / target_duration per call. head_offset uses ffmpeg-trim directly. tail_offset and target_duration probe the source via ffprobe-info first (so 2 payment tickets). target_duration > source_duration loops via ffmpeg-loop; ≤ source trims. AI-based extend (seedance-i2v continuation) is a separate director tool, not this one.

project_id.description: Project id (from generate_project / submit_creative_job).

head_offset.description: Seconds to trim from the start of the scene. Mutually exclusive with tail_offset and target_duration.

tail_offset.description: Seconds to trim from the end. Probes the source video duration via ffprobe-info first, then ffmpeg-trim. Mutually exclusive with head_offset and target_duration.

target_duration.description: Absolute new duration in seconds. If target_duration ≤ source duration, ffmpeg-trim trims to that length. If target_duration > source duration, ffmpeg-loop loops the source to the target. Mutually exclusive with head_offset and tail_offset.

annotations.title: Trim or extend a scene's duration

tools.name: director_variant
tools.title: Create a Named Variant Timeline of a Project
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants a NEW named cut of an existing project — e.g. '30s teaser', 'pitch cut', 'square format' — without losing the original. Creates a child project with parent_project_id link; the parent stays untouched (non-destructive). v1 takes an explicit scenes:[] index list in playback order. Natural-language intent picking ('lead with the climax') ships v2.

project_id.description: Parent project id.

name.description: Variant label (e.g. 'teaser_30s', 'pitch_cut'). Surfaced on the viewer to distinguish from the root.

scenes.description: Array of scene indices from the parent project, in playback order. Omit to copy all parent scenes verbatim (useful when the only change is the variant name).

title_override.description: Optional new title for the variant. Default: parent.title + ' — ' + name.

tools.name: director_reorder
tools.title: Reorder a Project's Scenes
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to change the PLAYBACK ORDER of existing scenes without re-rendering anything — e.g. 'move scene 4 before scene 2', 'lead with the last shot'. Pass the full new order as an old-index permutation: order:[2,0,3,1] means old scene 2 now plays first, old scene 0 second, etc. Scenes are re-indexed to their new position so later director_* calls addressing scenes by index stay consistent.

project_id.description: Project id (from generate_project / submit_creative_job).

order.description: Permutation of 0..N-1 (N = current scene count) — the NEW playback order. order[k] is the OLD scene index that should play at position k, e.g. order:[2,0,3,1] means old scene 2 now plays first.

tools.name: director_beat_lock
tools.title: Snap Scene Boundaries to a Beat Schedule
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user has a project + a music bed and wants scene cuts to land on beats — e.g. 'snap all cuts to the music at 120 BPM, 4 beats per scene'. v1 requires explicit BPM (audio detection deferred — chassis gap). Creates a variant project with target_duration_sec on each scene that future retime calls will conform to.

project_id.description: Parent project id.

bpm.description: Beats per minute. Range 40–240. v1 requires this explicit — automatic detection from audio_ref ships in v2.

beats_per_scene.description: Beats each scene holds for. Default 4. Higher = slower cut rhythm; lower = faster.

audio_ref.description: Optional reference to the audio track this BPM was measured against (e.g. '@aud-1' or an https URL). v1 records this in the variant's metadata but doesn't consume it. v2 will use it for the auto-BPM detection.

start_offset_sec.description: Optional offset into the audio where the beat schedule starts (default 0). Useful when the first scene should hit on a downbeat several seconds into the track.

annotations.title: Snap scene boundaries to a beat schedule

tools.name: director_export
tools.title: Stitch a Project + Run Its Brand Finishing Chain
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants a single final video of their project, optionally with a brand kit's deterministic finishing chain (watermark / aspect crop / audio mix / LUFS) applied. Stitches scenes via ffmpeg-concat, then runs each chain step sequentially. v1: kind:"mcp" publish bridges (slack-/drive-/linear-/notion-/github-) are SKIPPED with a warning — none are registered on the network yet; non-publish chain steps run fine.

project_id.description: Project to export. Variants (parent_project_id set) work too.

brand_kit_id.description: Optional Brand / Context Kit id. When set AND the kit has a finishing_chain, each step runs sequentially after the concat. Omit for a raw concat-only export.

soundtrack.description: 'auto' (default): if the project has no director_score bed, auto-generate one via sonilo-t2m (licensed instrumental) and mix it under the reel. 'off': skip any soundtrack for this export — including an existing director_score bed — without un-scoring the project.

annotations.title: Stitch a project + run its finishing chain

tools.name: assemble
tools.title: Assemble Your Own Clips Into an Editable Timeline
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user brings their OWN video/image clips (podcast, phone footage, lecture recording, stock) and wants to stitch / cut / edit them — the bring-your-own-footage editor. Registers each clip as a scene on a persistent project (optionally trimming per-clip in/out first via ffmpeg-trim), then returns a stitched preview. The project is then fully editable with director_retime / director_reorder / director_insert (splice in AI b-roll) / transcribe (captions) / director_export (final). Clips must be public https URLs — upload local files via `upload` first.

src.description: Public https URL of a video clip (or image). Upload a local file via `upload` / `create_upload_url` first, then pass its public URL here.

title.description: Optional label for this clip's scene (shown in the viewer).

in.description: Trim start, in seconds — drop everything before this point (video clips only).

out.description: Trim end, in seconds — drop everything after this point (video clips only).

type.description: Media type. Default: inferred from the URL extension. An 'image' clip is turned into a short motion clip (Ken Burns pan/zoom by default) so stills move on the timeline.

animate.description: For image clips: how to add motion. 'kenburns' (default) = deterministic ffmpeg pan/zoom — cheap, fast, no GPU. 'i2v' = AI image-to-video (pixverse-i2v) for organic motion — slower/costlier. Ignored for video clips.

direction.description: For Ken Burns image clips: pan/zoom direction (default 'in' = push-in). Ignored for i2v and video clips.

motion.description: For image clips animated via i2v: the motion/camera prompt (e.g. 'slow cinematic push-in'). Ignored for Ken Burns and video clips.

duration.description: For image clips: seconds of motion to generate (default 5). Ignored for video clips.

clips.description: Ordered clips to assemble into the timeline (top = first).

project_id.description: Append these clips to an existing project's timeline. Omit to create a new project.

title.description: Title for a new project (ignored when project_id is set).

music.description: Optional music-bed URL laid under the stitched preview (ffmpeg-mux, loop-filled to the video length so it never stops short). Generate one with create_media(action:'music') first.

transition.description: Transition between clips in the stitched preview. Default: cut.

stitch.description: Also return a stitched-preview MP4 of the whole timeline. Default true. The persistent project is created either way — set false to skip the extra ffmpeg-concat call.

annotations.title: Assemble your own clips into a timeline

tools.name: transcribe
tools.title: Transcribe Speech → Captions (SRT)
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants captions/subtitles for a video or audio clip from its own speech. Runs ASR (wizper) and returns the transcript text + timed SRT + cues. Set burn:true to also burn the captions onto the video (ffmpeg-burn-subtitles) and get a captioned video URL back. Pair with `assemble` for the caption-my-footage flow.

source_url.description: Public https URL of the video or audio to transcribe. For a video, the audio track is transcribed.

burn.description: If true, burn the timed captions onto the video and return the captioned video URL (requires a VIDEO source_url). Default false — returns transcript + SRT only.

language.description: Optional ISO language hint (e.g. 'en', 'es'). Omit to auto-detect.

granularity.description: Caption granularity. 'word' → per-word cues via whisper-word (the karaoke 'hit every word' effect). 'segment' (default) → phrase-level via wizper.

vocabulary.description: Proper nouns / brand names / jargon the ASR must spell correctly (e.g. ['Livepeer', 'Petkanics']). Routes transcription to the whisper capability, which accepts a vocabulary-bias prompt — the default wizper does NOT (verified against the provider schema), which is why brand names came back as 'LifePeer' / 'live peer' and query matches silently missed them. Use whenever a query term or caption must contain a specific name.

font_size.description: Burned caption font size in px (default 28). Only applies with burn:true.

font_color.description: Burned caption fill color — a name or hex, e.g. 'yellow' or '#F5E400' (default white). Only with burn:true.

outline.description: Burned caption outline/stroke thickness in px (default 2). Only with burn:true.

caption_position.description: Burned caption vertical position (default bottom). Only with burn:true.

tools.name: edit_clip
tools.title: Edit One Clip (reframe / stabilize / denoise / silence-cut / ken-burns)
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants a deterministic finishing edit on a single clip — reframe to a vertical/square aspect for social (op:'reframe'), stabilize shaky footage (op:'stabilize'), clean up noisy audio (op:'denoise'), trim dead air from the ends (op:'silence_cut'), or turn a still image into a pan/zoom motion clip (op:'kenburns'). Cheap, fast, GPU-free ffmpeg tool caps (~$0.0005/call). Returns the edited public URL — compose with `assemble` / `director_export`. Source must be a public https URL.

source_url.description: Public https URL of the clip to edit. For kenburns this is a still image; for the others it's a video.

op.description: The edit to apply: kenburns (still→motion), denoise (clean audio), stabilize (de-shake), reframe (aspect crop), silence_cut (trim dead air).

duration_sec.description: kenburns: output clip length in seconds (default 5).

bias.description: reframe: which part to keep when cropping (default 'top' — keeps faces in frame).

strength.description: denoise: FFT noise-reduction strength in dB (default 12).

smoothing.description: stabilize: camera-path smoothing window in frames (default 15; higher = smoother/more crop).

threshold_db.description: silence_cut: dB below which audio counts as silence (default -35).

min_silence_sec.description: silence_cut: minimum silence length to treat as dead air (default 0.6s).

pad_sec.description: silence_cut: seconds of padding to keep around detected speech (default 0.1s).

project_id.description: Optional. If given with scene_index, the edited clip is persisted in place onto that scene (the Studio 'edit this scene' flow). Omit to just return the edited URL for composing.

scene_index.description: Optional 0-based scene index to overwrite with the edited clip (requires project_id).

tools.name: clean_speech
tools.title: Tighten a Talk (remove pauses / cut phrases)
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to tighten spoken video — remove filler words (remove_fillers: um/uh/er/ah/hmm, word-level), remove dead-air pauses (停顿音, on by default), and/or cut specific sentences (remove_phrases, e.g. a flubbed line). Pass `fillers` to also cut risky words like 'like'/'so'. Source must be a public https video URL.

source_url.description: Public https URL of the video to tighten.

remove_fillers.description: Remove filler words (um, uh, er, ah, hmm…) using word-level speech timing. Default false.

fillers.description: Extra single-word fillers to also cut, added to the defaults — e.g. ["like","so","basically"]. Use with care: these words have legitimate uses too.

min_silence_sec.description: Remove internal pauses longer than this many seconds (default 0.6). Set 0 to skip pause removal.

remove_phrases.description: Sentences/phrases to cut out entirely, e.g. ["let me start over"]. Matched at sentence granularity.

pad_sec.description: Padding kept around each kept span so cuts breathe (default 0.1s).

project_id.description: Optional. With scene_index, persist onto that scene.

tools.name: overlay
tools.title: Overlay a Logo / Product / Lower-Third onto a Video
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to brand or annotate a video — drop a logo/watermark or a product image into a corner (pass image_url + position), OR add a branded text lower-third (pass name + optional title). One composite pass over live tool caps. Returns the composited URL; with project_id+scene_index it updates that scene in place. Source + image must be public https URLs.

source_url.description: Public https URL of the base video.

image_url.description: Logo / product / watermark image to overlay. Give this OR name (lower-third).

position.description: Corner for an image overlay (default bottom-right).

scale.description: Image overlay width relative to the video (default 0.2 = 20%).

padding.description: Image overlay margin from the edge in px (default 16).

x.description: Image overlay X position as a fraction of the frame (0=left, 1=right). Overrides position.

y.description: Image overlay Y position as a fraction of the frame (0=top, 1=bottom). Overrides position.

start_sec.description: Show the image overlay only from this time (seconds). Enables a timed PiP.

end_sec.description: Hide the image overlay after this time (seconds). Requires end_sec > start_sec.

track.description: Keyframed path [{t,x,y}] (t seconds, x/y normalized 0–1) the image overlay follows over time — a subject-tracked PiP. Supply this directly, or use track_sidecar_url to derive it.

track_sidecar_url.description: Public URL of a per-frame detections/track sidecar (from yolo-detect / supervision-track). The overlay's path is derived from the tracked subject's box centers.

track_class.description: With track_sidecar_url: which detected class to follow (e.g. 'person'). Omit to follow the highest-confidence subject.

name.description: Lower-third primary line (bold), e.g. a person's name. Give this OR image_url.

title.description: Lower-third secondary line (regular), e.g. a role.

project_id.description: Optional. With scene_index, persist the composited clip onto that scene.

tools.name: find_moments
tools.title: Analyze a Video — find what's in it & where
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user has a long/real video and wants to know what's in it or find a part — 'what's in this recording', 'find where she talks about pricing', 'break this into scenes'. Transcribes (wizper) into timed moments and best-effort adds visual scene/subject analysis (marlin-video). Pass `query` to filter to matching moments. Read-only; returns a moments list you can feed to trimming/clipping. This is the footage-intelligence foundation for auto-clipping.

source_url.description: Public https URL of the video to analyze.

query.description: Optional: only return moments whose speech/scene matches this, e.g. "pricing" or "the demo".

vocabulary.description: Proper nouns / brand names / jargon the ASR must spell correctly (e.g. ['Livepeer', 'Petkanics']). Routes transcription to the whisper capability, which accepts a vocabulary-bias prompt — the default wizper does NOT (verified against the provider schema), which is why brand names came back as 'LifePeer' / 'live peer' and query matches silently missed them. Use whenever a query term or caption must contain a specific name.

include_scenes.description: Also run visual scene/subject analysis (marlin-video), best-effort. Default true.

language.description: Optional ISO language hint for transcription.

annotations.title: Analyze a video — find what's in it

tools.name: autoclip
tools.title: Auto-clip a Long Video into Social Shorts
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user has a long video (podcast, webinar, interview, talk) and wants short social clips — 'turn this into shorts/clips for TikTok/Reels', 'give me the best moments as vertical clips'. Finds the best speech moments (find_moments), plans N clip windows, and renders each: trim → reframe (default 9:16) → burned captions. Returns N ready-to-post clip URLs. `count` default 3 (max 10). Long video → allow a couple minutes. COMPOSES with find_moments: pass its `moments` array through to clip exactly the moments you filtered (skips the internal re-analysis), or pass `query` to filter in one call.

source_url.description: Public https URL of the long video to clip.

count.description: How many clips to produce (default 3, max 10).

captions.description: Burn captions onto each clip (default true).

moments.description: Pre-selected transcript moments to clip from — pass find_moments' `moments` array through verbatim (same shape). When set, autoclip SKIPS its own transcription/moment pass entirely and plans clips from exactly this list. Use after filtering find_moments by query or by hand, so the clips cover the moments you chose rather than what an internal re-run happens to find.

query.description: Convenience filter when you have NOT pre-filtered: forwarded to the internal find_moments pass ('Livepeer', 'pricing'), so only matching moments are clipped. Ignored when `moments` is supplied. NOTE: matching is against the ASR transcript — proper nouns the ASR mangled will not match; for those, call find_moments + transcribe yourself, correct/inspect, then pass `moments`.

vocabulary.description: Forwarded to the internal find_moments pass: proper nouns the ASR must spell correctly (routes transcription to the whisper capability, which accepts a vocabulary bias). Pair with `query` so a brand-name query stops missing its own mangled mentions.

annotations.title: Auto-clip a long video into shorts

tools.name: extract_design_genome

Phase 1 of the Muse playbook. Deconstructs a reference into a structured, editable Design Genome (pacing, grade/palette, motion, type, sound) using marlin-video + transcribe. Read-only. REQUIRES rights_ack:true (confirm you may use the video as inspiration; Muse extracts abstract style, never reuses footage). Then elicit the user's goal/emphasize/avoid + their own materials and build with the existing render tools; run check_distinctiveness before publishing.

reference_url.description: Public https URL of the reference video to deconstruct.

rights_ack.description: Confirm you have the rights to use this video as INSPIRATION. Muse extracts abstract style (never reuses footage). Must be true to proceed.

annotations.title: Deconstruct a reference video into a genome

tools.name: check_distinctiveness
tools.title: Muse — Inspiration Firewall (is the output a copy?)
tools.description: USE WHEN: you have a Muse output and want to confirm it's INSPIRED BY the reference, not a clone — the final gate of the Muse playbook. Compares the reference Design Genome against a genome extracted from your generated output (palette/pacing/rhythm/motion) and returns a verdict: distinct | borderline | clone_risk. Read-only heuristic, no I/O. Get both genomes via extract_design_genome first.

candidate_genome.description: A DesignGenome extracted from YOUR generated output.

annotations.title: Inspiration firewall — is the output a copy?

tools.name: script_from_topic
tools.title: Idea / URL → Scripted Video
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants a video from an idea or a source page with no footage — 'make a 60s explainer about X', 'turn this blog post into a video' (pass its url). Optionally fetches the URL to GROUND the script in the real content, then writes scenes (Hermes auto-plan) and renders. Returns an async job_id — stream with subscribe_progress. Thin front-end over submit_creative_job.

topic.description: What the video is about, e.g. "our new pricing tiers". Give this and/or a url.

url.description: Optional source page to ground the script in (blog post, docs, announcement).

style.description: Optional visual style applied to every scene.

annotations.title: Idea or URL to scripted video

tools.name: generate_explainer
tools.title: Stock-B-roll Explainer Video (beats → search → concat → narrate → mix)
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants a quick explainer video from a list of beats — e.g. 'topic: how solar panels work, beats: sunlight hits the panel, photons knock electrons loose, electrons flow as DC current, inverter converts to AC, your house consumes the AC'. Each beat becomes a stock-footage search + a narration sentence. v1 requires explicit beats (auto-script from topic ships v2). Optional voice_id clones an existing voice library entry; default chatterbox voice otherwise. aspect controls the stock orientation filter. Pipeline = stock-search-video × N → ffmpeg-concat → chatterbox-tts → ffmpeg-mux; returns the final video URL. NOTE: requires production registration of stock-search-video + ffmpeg-concat + chatterbox-tts + ffmpeg-mux; fails fast with a capability_missing error if any are not yet live.

topic.description: Short headline describing the explainer's subject (used as the per-beat search query suffix to keep B-roll on-topic).

beats.description: Ordered plain-language script — one entry per shot, 2-8 entries total. Each becomes a stock-search-video query and a narration sentence. Keep each beat ~10-20 words for natural narration pacing.

voice_id.description: Optional voice library id (from voice_list). When set, the TTS step clones the voice via its source_audio_url. Omit to use the chatterbox-tts default voice.

aspect.description: Output aspect ratio. v1 only influences the stock-search-video orientation filter; absolute crop / scale is a v2 add-on through the brand_kit finishing chain.

tools.name: create_cad_model
tools.title: Text or image → 3D-printable STL (code-CAD)
tools.description: Turn a text brief OR a reference image (incl. an AI-generated image) into a 3D-PRINTABLE STL via parametric code-CAD (OpenSCAD) — clean, manifold, editable, slicer-ready geometry, NOT a messy AI mesh. Runs an author→render→critique→refine self-critique loop: writes OpenSCAD, renders a 4-view, compares it to the reference, and iterates until the part is watertight + manifold (the hard gate) and (for image runs) the shape matches. Returns the STL URL + the printability report + the editable OpenSCAD source. USE WHEN: the user wants a printable part, a 'picture → printable' conversion, a parametric bracket/holder/enclosure, or a manufacture-ready 3D model. For a visual/render-only 3D asset (game/AR) use tripo-i3d / triposplat instead. Requires the cad-render tool capability registered on the tool orch, and GEMINI_API_KEY on the MCP server for the authoring/critique LLM.

prompt.description: Text brief for the part, e.g. 'a parametric phone stand tilted 65° with a cable cutout, ~80mm wide'. Provide this and/or image_url.

image_url.description: Reference image (a photo or an AI-generated image) of the object to recreate as a printable part. The loop vision-analyzes it, writes OpenSCAD, renders a 4-view, and iterates until the shape matches. Provide this and/or prompt.

scad.description: Optional seed OpenSCAD source to start from (skips the initial LLM authoring pass). Useful to render hand-written code through the same printability gate.

max_iterations.description: Max author→render→critique→refine cycles. Default 3. Each cycle is 1 LLM authoring call + 1 render; image runs add 1 vision critique.

match_threshold.description: For image runs: minimum shape-match score (0..1) from the 4-view critique to accept. Default 0.7. Ignored for text-only runs (printability is the only gate then).

fn.description: OpenSCAD $fn facet count for curved surfaces. Default 64.

min_wall_mm.description: Minimum wall / feature thickness for the printability gate. Default 1.0mm.

max_dim_mm.description: Max bounding-box dimension on any axis (build-volume fit). Default 256mm.

tools.name: refine_cad_model
tools.title: Revise a CAD model from an instruction, re-gate it
tools.description: Revise an existing CAD part from a natural-language instruction (e.g. 'thicken walls to 2mm', 'add a 5mm hole through the center', 'make it 20% shorter'), then re-render it through the printability gate. Pass the OpenSCAD source from create_cad_model's structuredContent.scad plus the instruction. Returns the new STL + updated source. One edit per call — chain for multi-step changes.

scad.description: The current OpenSCAD source to revise (from create_cad_model's structuredContent.scad).

instruction.description: Natural-language change, e.g. 'thicken walls to 2mm', 'add a 5mm hole through the center', 'make it 20% shorter'.

image_url.description: Optional reference image to keep the revision aligned to.

min_wall_mm.description: Min wall for the gate. Default 1.0mm.

annotations.title: Revise a CAD model and re-gate it

tools.name: export_stl
tools.title: Check an STL is slicer-ready (printability gate)
tools.description: Validate an STL (by URL) against the printability gate: watertight, manifold (consistent winding), positive volume, body count, build-volume fit, and minimum wall/feature size. Returns {printable, issues, ...} and re-publishes the validated STL. USE WHEN: before slicing/printing, or to check an STL from anywhere — including an AI mesh cap (tripo-i3d), which typically FAILS watertight/manifold and shows why code-CAD is the manufacture-ready path.

stl_url.description: URL of the STL to validate.

max_dim_mm.description: Max bounding-box dimension on any axis (build-volume fit). Default 256mm.

expected_bodies.description: If set, flag the part as non-printable unless it has exactly this many disconnected bodies (usually 1).

tools.name: upload_image
tools.title: Upload an image so the tools can use it
tools.description:
Convert an image — a chat attachment OR any public URL — into a hosted URL the rest of the tools can use. Two ways: (1) attach the image inline in chat and the agent passes it as base64 (works up to ~1 MB before transport limits), or (2) paste any public URL (Imgur, Drive 'anyone with link', GitHub raw, etc.) and the server fetches and re-hosts it (up to 10 MB).

Use when the marketer says 'use this product photo', 'place this shoe in a different scene', or 'animate this image' and the image isn't already a public URL. If a chat-attachment upload fails ('base64 round-trip mismatch' or 'length not multiple of 4'), the transport is truncating — retry with a public URL instead. Pass the returned URL to place_subject or create_media. Free.

data.description: Base64-encoded image bytes (without `data:image/...;base64,` prefix). Use this when Claude has the image inline from a conversation attachment. **Note:** large images (≥1 MB) may hit MCP transport body limits and arrive truncated. If the upload fails with a base64-decode error, fall back to `source_url`.

source_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the image to re-host. **Use this whenever base64 is failing** or the image is already reachable on the public internet. The server fetches the URL, validates content-type + size, and re-hosts on Livepeer Agent storage. Imgur / Drive 'anyone with link' / GitHub raw / an existing generated-media URL all work; auth-walled services (private S3, Notion, Confluence) don't. Either `data` or `source_url` must be supplied.

mime_type.description: MIME type. Raster only (jpeg/png/webp/gif/avif/heic/heif). SVG and other XML-based formats are rejected — they can carry executable content in the app origin. Defaults to 'image/jpeg' for base64; for source_url the server reads it from the source's Content-Type header.

filename.description: Optional original filename for traceability — surfaces in storage logs but not in the returned URL.

annotations.title: Upload an image so the tools can use it

tools.name: upload
tools.title: Upload any file (image / video / audio) so the tools can use it
tools.description: Convert a file — a chat attachment (base64) OR any public URL — into a hosted https URL the rest of the tools can use as source_url / audio_url / video_url. Works for images, video, and audio (MIME auto-detected from a data: prefix, filename, or magic bytes). Two ways: (1) pass base64 inline (reliable up to ~3 MB before MCP transport limits; any size fails cleanly with a pointer to create_upload_url), or (2) pass any public URL and the server fetches + re-hosts it (up to 50 MB). SVG is rejected (XSS). Use when the user says 'use this clip/audio/photo' and it isn't already a public URL. For files larger than ~3 MB inline, use create_upload_url (signed PUT) or scripts/host-local-file.sh. Free.

data.description: Base64-encoded file bytes for ANY supported type (image / video / audio). A `data:<mime>;base64,` prefix is tolerated but not required. Large payloads (≥ ~3 MB) may hit MCP transport body limits and arrive truncated — for those use create_upload_url (signed PUT) or a public source_url instead.

source_url.description: Public https URL to re-host (image / video / audio). The server fetches, validates content-type + size (≤ 50 MB), and re-hosts on Livepeer Agent storage. Use this whenever base64 fails or the file is already reachable. Either `data` or `source_url` is required.

mime_type.description: Optional explicit MIME (e.g. 'video/mp4', 'audio/mpeg', 'image/png'). If omitted it's detected from a data: prefix, the filename extension, or the file's magic bytes. SVG and non-media types are rejected.

kind.description: Optional hint for the media family. Purely advisory — the resolved MIME determines the actual kind returned.

filename.description: Optional original filename — used for extension-based MIME detection and storage traceability.

annotations.title: Upload any file so the tools can use it

tools.name: create_upload_url
tools.title: Get a signed URL to upload a large file (image / video / audio)
tools.description: Return a one-time signed PUT URL + headers for uploading a LARGE local file (up to 50 MB) that's too big for inline base64 (which caps near ~3 MB) and isn't already a public URL. Meant for capable clients with a shell (Codex / Cursor): call this with content_type (or kind), PUT your bytes to the returned upload_url with the returned headers (a ready-to-run `curl` recipe is included), then pass the returned public_url as source_url / video_url / audio_url to create_media etc. Claude Desktop (no shell) can't PUT directly — drag the file into the webapp or use the `livepeer upload` CLI. For files > 50 MB use scripts/host-local-file.sh. Free.

content_type.description: MIME type of the file you will upload, e.g. 'video/mp4', 'image/png', 'audio/mpeg'. Either content_type or kind is required.

kind.description: Media family shortcut when you don't know the exact MIME (image→image/png, video→video/mp4, audio→audio/mpeg). content_type wins if both are set.

filename.description: Optional original filename; used to keep the extension readable in the hosted URL.

size.description: Optional file size in bytes; rejected early if it exceeds the 50 MB cap.

annotations.title: Get a signed URL to upload a large file

tools.name: request_upload
tools.title: Ask the user for a photo/video via an upload link (phone-friendly)
tools.description: Mint a 30-minute upload link the USER opens on any device — phone photo album, phone camera, or desktop — to send you a file at FULL quality (up to 50 MB; iPhone HEIC converts automatically; nothing is resized). Use whenever the user wants to work with a picture/clip you cannot reach: a chat-pasted image (vision-only — you can never recover its bytes), a photo on their phone, or any file on a client with no shell. Show the returned page_url to the user, then call get_upload with the returned token to collect the hosted URL for create_media (animate / i2i / upscale / restyle). Never ask the user to downscale or re-send a photo inline. Free.

kind.description: What the user is expected to send — narrows the page's file picker. Default 'any'.

annotations.title: Ask the user for a photo/video via an upload link

tools.name: get_upload
tools.title: Collect the file the user uploaded via request_upload
tools.description: Wait (up to ~20s per call) for the upload session from request_upload to complete, then return the hosted https URL plus mime/size/dimensions — pass it as source_url / video_url / audio_url to create_media and friends. status 'pending' means the user is still choosing a file: re-call silently with the same token (don't show the token; re-share the page_url if they seem stuck). 'expired' means mint a fresh link with request_upload. Free.

wait_seconds.description: How long to hold this call open waiting for the upload (default 20s — well inside MCP tool timeouts). The user is picking a photo on their phone, so one or two held calls usually suffice; re-call while status is 'pending'.

annotations.title: Collect the file the user uploaded via request_upload

Turn a still into a clip first with create_media({action:'animate', source_url:<still>}).

logo_url.description: Public URL of the EXACT logo asset (SVG / transparent PNG preferred).

corners.description: KEYSTONE — where the asset's four corners land, as [x,y] FRACTIONS of the frame (0-1), in order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. This is the transform for a screen or surface seen at an angle: read the corners of the target surface straight off the plate. Use this instead of rotate_y_deg for any real photograph — a surface seen from one side has two vertical edges of DIFFERENT lengths, which a symmetric rotation cannot produce. Takes precedence over curve_deg.

curve_deg.description: Total horizontal arc, in degrees, that the asset BENDS through (0 = flat, the default). This is what puts a label on a can or a UI on a curved monitor — rotate_y_deg only tilts a flat plane, which can never follow a curve. Try 12–30 for a curved monitor, 90–160 for the visible face of a can or bottle. Pair with curve_dir.

curve_dir.description: Which way it bends. 'convex' (default) bulges toward the viewer — a can, a bottle, a ball. 'concave' recedes in the middle and comes forward at the edges — a curved monitor.

sheen.description: Strength of a soft highlight laid over the asset, 0-0.6 (default 0). The overlay is OPAQUE, so it erases whatever glare the plate painted on the glass and the asset can read as pasted-on. 0.10-0.18 is enough for a screen behind a window; skip it for a matte surface. Deterministic — a CSS gradient cannot alter a character.

tools.name: set_active_brand_kit
tools.title: Pin a Brand Kit so every image stays on-brand
tools.description:
Pin a Brand Kit for the next hour so every image, video, and moodboard the marketer asks for stays automatically on-brand — palette and style words inherited without re-typing. Auto-clears after 60 minutes or when the marketer says 'switch brands' / 'unpin'. Verifies the kit exists before pinning so dead references can't carry forward.

Use right after brand_kit_create, or after listing kits with brand_kit_list. Free to call — this just sets the default.

kit_id.description: Brand kit / ContextKit id to lock onto. Get from brand_kit_create or context_kit_list. The kit must exist under your bearer; non-existent kits are rejected here so the agent doesn't ship a dead reference.

tools.name: get_active_brand_kit
tools.title: Check which Brand Kit is currently pinned
tools.description: Show which Brand Kit is currently pinned for this session, or 'nothing pinned' if the marketer hasn't picked one yet. Use at the start of a chat to remind yourself of the active brand before generating anything. Free.

annotations.title: Check which brand kit is pinned

tools.name: clear_active_brand_kit
tools.title: Unpin the current Brand Kit (start a fresh brand context)
tools.description: Unpin the current Brand Kit so the next set of images runs without any brand defaults. Use when the marketer switches campaigns mid-chat ('now let's do a different brand') or wants a fresh start. Free.

tools.name: moodboard_create
tools.title: Start a new moodboard for a brand or campaign
tools.description:
Create an empty moodboard tied to a Brand Kit. Free to create — this just sets up the container so the next step (moodboard_spread) knows what brand to lock onto. Returns a moodboard_id you'll pass to spread, refine, and publish.

Use when the marketer asks for a moodboard, launch board, look-and-feel exploration, or stakeholder share.

intent.description: One-line creative brief. Marketer: 'premium-but-warm Aurora X1 launch with soft amber tones'. Community organizer: 'promote our community garden — intergenerational, welcoming'. Game studio: 'second-act dungeon mood, candlelit, weight-of-history'.

context_kit_id.description: Optional ContextKit. When set, palette + reference imagery + skill packs come from the kit and the board is brand-locked. Omit for unbranded exploration.

tools.name: moodboard_spread
tools.title: Render the moodboard images (palette-locked, premium models)
tools.description:
Render 2–30 moodboard images in parallel using premium image models (nano-banana, recraft-v4, flux-dev, gemini-image; gpt-image is available via model_overrides for its stylization fidelity but is kept out of the auto-pool as the slowest cap). Every slot stays on the Brand Kit's palette and style. Cost is roughly $0.05–$0.10 per slot — a 6-slot board lands at $0.30–$0.60, a 12-slot at $0.60–$1.20. Built-in spend cap (default $5.00) rejects up-front if your slot list would exceed it. Returns each slot's URL plus a short reference so the marketer can call back later to refine specific slots.

ASYNC HANDLE: premium/large boards (slow-cap pool such as recraft-v4/gpt-image, or count ≥ 12) return in <1s with status:'rendering' and a job_id — the render continues server-side and NEVER gets lost to a client-side timeout. Poll it with subscribe_progress({ job_id: moodboard_id }) in a loop until status is 'done' or 'partial', or open the returned viewer_url (updates live as slots land). Small/fast boards return inline with image previews. Pass async:true to force the handle from any client with a short tool-call timeout, or async:false to force blocking inline.

USE WHEN: brand exploration, launch deck, campaign discovery — N parallel images locked to a Brand Kit, no narrative ordering. For ordered narrative scenes (story, film) use generate_project. For 'every slot must show the same product in a different scene' use place_subject. For 2–8 stylistic variations of one existing image use create_variations. On 12+ slot boards, mix 70% on-brand + 30% adjacent-but-coherent so stakeholders can actually choose between directions.

count.description: How many slots to generate (2–30). Defaults to 12 in the docs but caller picks. Cost scales linearly with count.

anchors.description: Optional reference image URLs the agent injects as anchors. The board still varies across slots, but each slot can lean toward one anchor's vibe.

subjects.description: Optional per-slot SUBJECTS, rotated across the board. Without this every slot renders the board's single intent and only the style varies — a spread of one idea in N treatments, which is what a moodboard usually means. Pass subjects when you want N different things instead: ['the hero pack shot','a hand holding it','the storefront']. Rotated by index, so 3 subjects across 12 slots gives each one four treatments.

styles.description: Optional explicit style hints rotated across slots ('70s film grain', 'soft watercolor', 'documentary photography'). When omitted, the agent picks from the active skill pack.

max_cost_usd.description: Pre-flight USD cap on the total spread (sum across all slots). Default $5.00 when omitted. Estimated via the live pricing metadata.

model_overrides.description: Optional explicit capability pool — round-robined across slots in the order given (e.g. ['gpt-image', 'recraft-v4']). When set, overrides the domain-default pool. Use this to explicitly include slow-premium models the auto-pool excludes (gpt-image — ~165s/slot, highest cost, best stylization fidelity for brand-name aesthetics). Omit for the curator's curated mix.

auto_publish.description: When true (default) the board auto-publishes after the spread completes — the viewer URL works immediately, the marketer can share it without an extra moodboard_publish call. Set to false to keep the board as a draft (status='draft') so you can inspect it before sharing — useful for review workflows where the marketer wants to vet slots before they go live.

confirm.description: Cost-preview safety latch (H1). Default `true` — runs the spread. Set to `false` for a dry-run that returns the estimated total, per-slot cost, capability pool, and expected wall-clock — without firing any inference. Pair with the agent prompt 'this will cost ~$X, proceed?' before committing to long premium spreads.

async.description: Return an async handle immediately instead of blocking until every slot renders. Default is auto: a board whose pool includes a slow cap (recraft-v4, gpt-image) or with count ≥ 12 returns a handle in <1s and renders server-side — poll it with subscribe_progress({ job_id: moodboard_id }); small/fast boards return inline with image previews. Pass true to force the handle (recommended for any client with a short tool-call timeout — the render never gets lost to a client-side timeout), or false to force blocking inline.

tools.name: moodboard_publish
tools.title: Publish the moodboard to a shareable link
tools.description:
Turn the moodboard into a public viewer URL the marketer can paste into Slack, email, or a deck. The viewer page shows the palette swatches and brand reference panel so stakeholders see the context, not just images. Default link lifetime is 14 days; max 90. Prompts are visible by default — pass an option to hide them for confidential briefs. Free.

Use at the end of the moodboard flow when the marketer asks for a link, share, deck, or 'send this to the team'.

include_prompts.description: Whether per-slot prompts are visible on the public viewer. Default true for transparency. Set false for confidential briefs.

expires_in_days.description: Share-URL validity window. Default 14 days, max 90.

annotations.title: Publish the moodboard to a link

tools.name: refine_slot
tools.title: Tweak one moodboard image (warmer, more cinematic, etc.)
tools.description:
Re-run a single moodboard slot with a tweak — 'warmer', 'vertical', 'more cinematic', 'less text', 'real photo not illustration'. Costs roughly the same as one image (~$0.05–$0.10) since it's a surgical edit; the rest of the board stays as-is. The previous version is kept (up to 5 history entries per slot) so you can revert if the tweak misses.

Use when the marketer says 'slot 3 needs to be warmer' or '@slot-2 try this with less polish'.

moodboard_id.description: Moodboard the slot lives in — from moodboard_create / spread.

slot_id.description: Slot identifier within the moodboard, e.g. 'slot-3'. Format matches the @-mention slug the spread response surfaces.

hint.description: Short refinement instruction in plain English — 'warmer', 'vertical orientation', 'more cinematic', 'remove the text overlay'. Blended into the original slot prompt; the model interprets the merged prompt for the re-render.

model_override.description: Optional capability override for the re-render. Defaults to the slot's current capability so the refinement preserves the model's stylistic signature.

tools.name: cancel_moodboard
tools.title: Stop a moodboard mid-render
tools.description: Stop a moodboard that's still rendering. Flips the board to 'cancelled' and discards any images that finish after this call. Already-finished slots stay visible. Use when the marketer says 'stop' or 'cancel that' mid-spread, or realises the brief was wrong. Honest limit: in-flight network requests already on the wire to fal complete, but their results are dropped rather than persisted. Free; safe to call twice.

moodboard_id.description: The moodboard to cancel. Same id format moodboard_create / moodboard_spread surface.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason the user is cancelling ('costing too much', 'wrong direction', 'time pressure'). Recorded on the board for future audit; surfaced in the cancel response.

tools.name: apply_template
tools.title: Apply a starter template to create a moodboard
tools.description:
Turn a MOODBOARD brief starter plus a few variables (brand name, product, audience) into a ready-to-render moodboard. Missing pieces fall back to sensible defaults. After this you'll have a moodboard_id and a one-click 'render the images' next step with the cost preview attached.

Use right after list_templates once the marketer has picked a starter. Free to apply — image rendering happens in the next step. NOT for the priced creative presets (camera moves / formats / looks) — those are catalog recipes, applied with apply_recipe.

template_id.description: Template identifier from `list_templates`. Each template carries a curated brief + style list + suggested slot count.

variables.description: Slot fills for the template. Each template's response lists its required slots (e.g. {product: 'Aurora X1', audience: 'EV-curious millennials', aesthetic: 'premium-warm'}). Missing slots fall back to the template's placeholder defaults so the call never errors out — the user just gets a less-tailored brief.

context_kit_id.description: Optional ContextKit to link the resulting moodboard to. When set, palette + reference imagery + skill packs come from the kit AND the template's style-list is merged on top.

tools.name: place_subject
tools.title: Place a product photo into different scenes (preserves the product)
tools.description:
Take one product or subject photo plus a list of scenarios, render each scene with the product placed naturally — shape, color, materials, and logos stay intact across every render. Uses Google's image-edit model, best-in-class for subject preservation. Cost is about $0.15–$0.25 per scene. If you don't supply scenes, picks 6 varied ones (outdoor / indoor / studio / atmospheric / seasonal). The subject-preservation prompt prelude is added automatically — no manual prompt engineering needed.

USE WHEN: 'put this product in 6 different settings', 'show this character across scenes', 'show our shoe in different lifestyles' — a single fixed subject across many scenes. For varying STYLE not scene use create_variations. For brand-exploration boards (different subjects allowed) use moodboard_spread. For an ordered narrative with characters that may evolve use generate_project. For 6+ scenes, wrap in moodboard_create + moodboard_spread first to get a shareable viewer URL.

source_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the source product/subject image. Required when `lora` is omitted — the agent injects this as image_url to the editing model so the subject's identity (shape, color, logos, materials) is preserved. When a `lora` is supplied, source_url is ignored (the LoRA carries the identity).

scenes.description: Optional explicit list of scene descriptions. One image per entry, generated in parallel. When omitted, the agent picks `count` default scenes from a curated archetype list (outdoor / indoor / studio / atmospheric / seasonal).

count.description: How many scenes to generate when `scenes` is omitted. Default 6. Cost scales linearly with count.

subject_hint.description: Optional anchor for the model (e.g. 'vintage road bike', 'white ceramic mug'). Helps when the source photo has multiple objects.

model_override.description: Editing model. Default 'nano-banana' (Google Imagen Edit — best subject identity preservation among image-edit models). 'kontext-edit' for heavier stylization. 'gpt-image-edit' when adding text/UI around the subject. **For high-fidelity product marketing**, pass `lora_id` instead — a trained LoRA on the product preserves brand text + frame geometry that image-edit models can't (they hallucinate wordmarks ~90% of the time).

lora.description: Optional trained LoRA for high-fidelity product / character preservation. When set, every scene routes through `flux-dev` + this LoRA instead of an image-edit + source_url — which is the right path for product marketing where wordmarks / frame geometry / decals must be accurate. Image-edit models (nano-banana, kontext-edit) hallucinate brand text ~90% of the time; a trained LoRA injects identity deterministically. Workflow: call list_loras to find an existing LoRA for the product, or submit_lora_train with 5–10 reference images (~$10, ~20 min) to create one. Then pass {weights_url, trigger, scale?} here. Trigger is auto-prepended to each scene's prompt; scale defaults to 0.7.

max_cost_usd.description: Optional per-call USD cap forwarded to create_media. Without it, the cost gate is disabled.

confirm.description: Cost-preview safety latch (H1). Default `true` — runs the fan-out. Set to `false` for a dry-run that returns the per-scene cost, model, and total estimate without firing inference.

annotations.title: Place a product photo into new scenes

tools.name: create_variations
tools.title: Make 2–8 stylistic variations of one image
tools.description:
Generate 2–8 variations of an existing image without re-typing the brief. Pick how you want to vary: 'seed' (different rolls of the same model, preserves composition), 'prompt' (style swaps like watercolor / oil / pencil), 'model' (rotate across image-edit models for the widest stylistic range), or 'mixed' (a balanced blend, the default). Cost is roughly $0.05–$0.10 per variation. Returns the variations plus a 'pick a favorite' menu so the marketer can animate it, place it elsewhere, or vary it further.

USE WHEN: 'give me 4 options', 'try this in watercolor and oil and pencil', 'a few alternatives, I'll pick one' — same composition, vary the style or seed. For the same subject in different SCENES use place_subject. For tweaking one moodboard slot toward a target (warmer, more cinematic) use refine_slot. For brand-exploration boards with different subjects allowed use moodboard_spread.

source_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the image to vary. The variations preserve compositional identity; they explore alternate seeds / prompts / models.

count.description: How many variations to produce. Default 4. Hard cap at 8 — beyond that you want a moodboard, not a variation set.

mode.description: Variation strategy. 'seed' = same model, different seeds (lowest stylistic drift). 'prompt' = same model, prompt rewritten with style keyword swaps. 'model' = same prompt, rotated across image-edit caps (widest range). 'mixed' = sensible blend (default).

prompt.description: Optional anchor prompt describing what to preserve. When omitted, the variations use a neutral 'maintain composition' prompt that lets the model interpret freely. Recommended: 1 short sentence naming the subject.

model_overrides.description: Explicit pool of image-edit capabilities for mode='model' or 'mixed'. Default pool: nano-banana → kontext-edit → gpt-image-edit → flux-fill (different stylistic signatures).

max_cost_usd.description: Per-call USD cap (sum across all variations). Default $2 — variations are cheap enough that the cap is mostly safety, not a real budget gate.

confirm.description: Cost-preview safety latch (H1). Default `true` — runs the variations. Set to `false` for a dry-run that returns the per-variation cost, mode mix, and capability pool without firing inference.

annotations.title: Make stylistic variations of one image

tools.name: convert
tools.title: Convert an Asset Between Canonical Formats
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user (or a downstream tool) needs an asset in a different format — mesh glb↔fbx↔obj↔usdz, CAD step↔stl↔3mf↔glb, image png↔exr↔jpg↔webp↔tiff. Two modes: pass project_id + scene_index to convert a project scene (appends a NEW lineage-linked scene; original stays), OR pass source_url (+ optional from) to convert any hosted asset one-shot — e.g. a create_cad_model STL → STEP. Surfaces an honest warning on any lossy conversion. Goes straight to the deterministic format-convert tool cap.

project_id.description: Project id holding the source asset (with scene_index). Omit to convert a raw source_url.

scene_index.description: Zero-based index of the scene to convert. Used with project_id.

source_url.description: A public asset URL to convert directly — e.g. a create_cad_model STL, or any hosted file — when it isn't a project scene. One-shot (returns the converted URL); pass project_id too to also append the result as a lineage scene.

from.description: Source format of source_url if its extension is ambiguous (e.g. 'stl').

to.description: Target format extension, e.g. glb | fbx | usd | usdz | stl | step | png | exr | jpg. Must be a supported target for the asset's kind.

max_cost_usd.description: Optional hard cap on the conversion cost in USD (forwarded to the cap).

return_file.description: Ask the cap to return the converted file inline (default: hosted URL).

tools.name: refine_3d
tools.title: Make a Mesh Production-Ready (decimate / UV / normals)
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to optimize or game-ready a 3D mesh asset — 'make it low-poly', 'decimate to 5k tris', 'clean UVs', 'bake normals'. Runs the deterministic blender-headless tool cap and appends a NEW lineage-linked mesh (the source stays). Mesh assets only (create_media + tripo-i3d makes one first). Tri budget is read from the instruction or defaulted per role.

project_id.description: Project id holding the mesh to refine.

scene_index.description: Zero-based index of the mesh scene.

instruction.description: What to do, e.g. 'game-ready: ≤5k tris, clean UVs', 'lower poly', 'decimate to 1200 tris', 'bake normals'.

max_cost_usd.description: Optional hard cap on the refine cost in USD (forwarded to the cap).

tools.name: handoff
tools.title: Hand an Asset Off to a Pro Tool (interop manifest)
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants to take a project asset into a pro tool — Godot / Unreal / Unity / Blender / FreeCAD. Emits a PUBLIC interop manifest (stable asset URL + format + full lineage + per-engine import hints) that a community bridge consumes to import the asset. This is how the spine reaches local tools without owning them. Targets: godot, unreal, unity, blender, freecad, generic.

project_id.description: Project id holding the asset.

scene_index.description: Zero-based scene index of the asset to hand off.

to.description: Target tool: godot | unreal | unity | blender | freecad | generic.

tools.name: asset_lineage
tools.title: Show an Asset's Provenance Chain
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user asks 'how was this made' / 'what's this derived from' / wants the provenance of an asset. Returns the lineage root→current (e.g. concept image → tripo mesh → game-ready decimate), with the op + cap at each step.

tools.name: import_asset
tools.title: Import an External Asset into a Project (with lineage)
tools.description: USE WHEN: you need to bring a generated or external asset URL into a project as a scene — e.g. a tripo-i3d mesh produced from a concept image, an uploaded model, or any hosted file — and optionally record what it derived from (derived_from = the source scene's index). This is what lets asset_lineage / handoff trace a full chain (concept image → mesh → game-ready), not just the last edit.

project_id.description: Project to import the asset into.

source_url.description: Public URL of the asset to import (mesh / image / cad / etc.).

kind.description: Asset kind. Inferred from format/URL/capability if omitted.

format.description: Format extension if the URL has none (e.g. 'glb').

capability.description: Producing capability hint (e.g. 'tripo-i3d') — used to infer kind when the URL has no extension.

derived_from.description: Zero-based index of the scene this asset was derived from — records lineage (parent_asset_id).

tools.name: create_cad_step
tools.title: Parametric CAD → native STEP (BREP solid)
tools.description: USE WHEN: the user wants an EDITABLE CAD part / a real STEP file for a CAD tool or manufacturing — not just a printable mesh. Authors CadQuery (OpenCASCADE BREP, the FreeCAD-family kernel) from a brief and exports a TRUE parametric STEP solid + a preview STL + a validation report. Pass `code` to skip authoring, or `code`+`instruction` to refine. This is the parametric complement to create_cad_model (OpenSCAD → mesh STL); use that for quick printable meshes, this for editable solids / STEP interchange.

prompt.description: What to model, e.g. 'wall bracket, 80×40×5mm base, 30mm wall, four M4 holes, filleted'. Omit if passing code.

code.description: CadQuery Python that assigns the solid to `result`. Skips authoring. With `instruction`, it's refined first.

instruction.description: Revision instruction applied to `code` (e.g. 'thicken the wall to 8mm, add a 10mm boss').

tolerance.description: STL tessellation tolerance for the preview mesh (mm). Default 0.1.

tools.name: demo_register
tools.title: Register for early access
tools.description: Capture an email (and optional use case) for early access to the platform. No API key required — this is the growth funnel's front door for anonymous/demo callers. Free.

tools.name: request_activation
tools.title: Request an activation code by email
tools.description: Send a one-time activation code by email. Pass `email` for a single recipient (no API key required — the keyless self-serve front door), OR pass `emails` (a list) to send codes to many recipients at once (marketer key required). Call activate with the code to unlock activated status. Free.

tools.name: activate
tools.title: Activate with a code
tools.description: Redeem a one-time activation code sent by request_activation. No API key required. On success, unlocks activated status for that email (and, for keyless demo callers, this IP). Free.

tools.name: me
tools.title: Get my profile
tools.description: Return your own profile (name/use case/email, if set) plus your resolved key class. Self-scoped — only ever reads the calling principal's own record. No role required. Free.

tools.name: me_usage
tools.title: Get my usage report
tools.description: Return your own aggregated usage (total calls, ok/failed counts, top capabilities/tools) over a time window (24h/7d/30d/all). Self-scoped — only ever reads the calling principal's own event ledger. detail:'full' adds a self-contained report_html for a render-as-PDF/HTML flow. No role required. Free.

period.description: Time window for the report. Defaults to 14d, the default ledger's retention. A window longer than the underlying source retains is CLAMPED (and says so) rather than reported as a confidently wrong total.

detail.description: 'summary' (default) caps the row list to the top 10. 'full' returns every row plus a self-contained report_html string, for a render-as-PDF/HTML flow.

tools.name: signup
tools.title: Sign up with your email
tools.description: Send yourself a one-time email verification code to start signing up (no API key required). Call signup_confirm with the code once it arrives to finish creating your account. Free.

tools.name: signup_confirm
tools.title: Confirm signup with your code
tools.description: Redeem the one-time code sent by signup. No API key required. On success, creates your own profile and mints you a PRODUCT key (via the configured KeyMintProvider — 'console' by default, which returns a synthetic pk_console_... test key; set KEY_MINT_PROVIDER=daydream, plus its endpoint config, for a real mint once that endpoint is confirmed). The raw key is shown exactly once — save it immediately. Self-scoped — only ever creates/updates the calling principal's own profile and key. Free.
